title: France's Unprecedented Supermarket Refrigerator Hacks Make It Europe's Most Hacked Country
content: The “unprecedented” hacks of French supermarket refrigerators have joined a series of major cyberattacks, making France the most hacked country in Europe, analysts say. Cyberattacks are rising worldwide, yet France remains a frequent target.
summary: The hacks of French supermarket refrigerators were described as unprecedented and are part of a series of major cyberattacks that have made France the most hacked country in Europe, according to some analysts. Cyberattacks are rising globally, and the article questions why France is such a ready target.
author: France 24

title: Italian schools evacuated after hoax bomb threats, PM Meloni says no concrete danger
content: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain and Ireland, which reportedly prompted some evacuations in Scotland. Meloni said she had called a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs for Wednesday to discuss the threats. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
summary: Schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after a series of hoax bomb threats. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no concrete danger and called a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs to discuss the threats.
author: France 24

title: Tens of thousands gather in Warsaw for Independence Day march days after Krakow shooting
content:
Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathizers gathered in Warsaw on Wednesday for the annual Independence Day March, held just days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow. The event takes place each November 11 to commemorate the end of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia, and Austria in 1918.

The march serves as a gathering point for various factions within Poland's right wing, including conservative-nationalists aligned with the Law and Justice (PiS) party, as well as far-right and radical groups. The event was covered by FRANCE 24’s Carys Garland.
summary: Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathisers gathered in Warsaw on Wednesday for the annual Independence Day March. The march took place days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow and draws participants from across Poland's right wing, including groups aligned with the Law and Justice party.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Linked to China Spy Allegations Over Chip Smuggling
content:
China has accused Nvidia of having a vulnerability at its core that could be exploited, according to the report. The allegation comes amid scrutiny of the company’s operations in China, where the firm dominates more than two‑thirds of the world’s AI computing power production.

Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with Singapore‑based Chinese tech CEO Alice Huang—who is not related to him. Huang is currently under investigation for purchasing Nvidia’s latest chips, which authorities suspect may have been smuggled back to mainland China illegally.

The article will explore the rise and possible fall of the Taiwan‑born AI icon, examining how these controversies could impact his standing in the industry.
summary: China accuses Nvidia of exploiting a vulnerability involving the purchase of state‑of‑the‑art chips that may have been smuggled back to mainland China. Jensen Huang admits an extramarital affair with Singapore‑based Chinese tech CEO Alice Huang, who is under scrutiny for the chip purchase.
author: France 24

title: Reporters Without Borders calls for release of French reporter Christophe Gleizes in Algeria
content: After being detained for almost 500 days in Algeria, Christophe Gleizes is no closer to being freed. Those close to him, as well as his fellow sports journalists have campaigned tirelessly for his release with the affair even attracting the attention of Zinedine Zidane, manager of the French football team. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Thibault Bruttin, Director General of Reporters Without Borders. He says that Gleizes has probably become "a token in a diplomatic game that we don't totally understand, that we don't totally master, up to the point where we are asking ourselves 'has he become a state hostage?'".
summary: Christophe Gleizes has been detained in Algeria for almost 500 days and remains unreleased. Reporters Without Borders' Director General Thibault Bruttin said he may have become a diplomatic hostage, as fellow journalists and football manager Zinedine Zidane have campaigned for his freedom.
author: France 24

title: France bans Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan from entering country
content: French authorities compelled Yossi Dagan, head of the Samaria Regional Council, to leave France after he arrived at a Paris airport last week, his office said in a statement on Wednesday. The French foreign ministry did not confirm that he was deported, but said Dagan is banned from French territory because of his involvement in Israel’s illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank. The ministry’s comment linked the ban directly to his settlement activities.
summary: French authorities forced Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan to leave France after he landed at a Paris airport last week. The French foreign ministry said Dagan is banned from French territory because of his involvement in Israel's illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, without confirming his deportation.
author: France 24

title: 17-year-old Gladbach forward Wael Mohya earns first Germany call-up
content: At 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first call‑up to the German national team. The dual‑national player has opted to follow the DFB route for now and, according to the announcement, could soon set a modern national‑team record.
summary: Wael Mohya, a 17-year-old Gladbach forward, has earned his first call-up to the Germany national team. The dual‑national talent has chosen the DFB path and could soon make modern national‑team history.
author: DW World

title: AIIB grievance mechanism faces hurdles, critics call for reforms
content: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) operates a grievance redress mechanism intended for individuals and communities impacted by its financed projects. However, the source notes that filing a complaint involves significant hurdles, prompting critics to call for reforms and greater transparency in the process.
summary: The AIIB has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. Critics say those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles and that reforms and greater transparency are needed.
author: DW World

title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, finds no deliberate election bias
content: Brazil’s electoral court imposed a fine on Meta after a complaint was filed by President Luiz Inácio Lula’s coalition. The court said it found no evidence that Meta intended to influence the election. Meta responded that it will contest the charge, calling the allegations false.
summary: Brazil's electoral court fined Meta after President Lula's coalition filed a complaint, but said there was no evidence of intent to influence the election. Meta said it will defend itself against false allegations.
author: DW World

title: Australian PM Anthony Albanese omits fossil fuels in UN climate summit speech
content:
During a historic address at the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese emphasized that governments have a “solemn responsibility” to act on climate change. He highlighted Australia’s progress in renewable energy but did not mention the fossil fuels that are driving the crisis.

The speech drew criticism for overlooking the country’s large coal industry. Albanese arrived in Antalya on Wednesday morning, where COP31 is being hosted by Turkey and presided over by his climate change minister, Chris Bowen.
summary: Australian PM Anthony Albanese omits fossil fuels in UN climate summit speech.
author: Guardian World

title: Finland's Canberra embassy Instagram staff‑training post goes viral
content: Finland’s embassy in Canberra was temporarily closed on Tuesday, a move that reportedly upset millions of people worldwide. After a promotion for a “Finnish Dinner Date” gained modest online attention, the embassy’s next Instagram post – showing a staff training day – unexpectedly went viral, surprising the diplomatic team.
summary: The Finnish embassy in Canberra shared a staff‑training‑day video on Instagram that attracted widespread attention. The embassy was temporarily closed on Tuesday, prompting upset among millions of people worldwide.
author: Guardian World

title: First Covid lockdowns, then alcohol to your door: rise in young Victorians with liver diseases prompts fears
content:
Young Victorians are drinking less overall, yet a small minority are consuming large, damaging amounts of alcohol, an expert notes. This trend has coincided with a rise in hospitalisations for severe, irreversible liver disease among young people, while alcohol‑related admissions remain above pre‑pandemic levels even after peaking during Covid lockdowns.

A new report from the Burnet Institute, commissioned by the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education (Fare), analysed nearly two decades of Victorian health data. The study examined the prevalence of alcohol‑associated harm, highlighting the growing concern over liver disease in younger populations.
summary: First Covid lockdowns, then alcohol to your door: rise in young Victorians with liver diseases prompts fears.
author: Guardian World

title: David Walliams removed from Australian film and publicity after harassment allegations
content:
Transmission Films, the distributor of the upcoming Australian fantasy film Fing!, has announced that David Walliams will be removed from the movie and its publicity campaign. Walliams, a children’s author and comedian who co‑wrote the film based on his own book, will no longer appear in the film or participate in media events ahead of its 14 January cinema debut.

The decision follows sexual‑harassment allegations that were made public. Walliams was accused of using his celebrity status to prey on young women for sex, prompting the distributors to cut his cameo and withdraw him from promotional activities.

The film’s release will proceed without Walliams’ involvement, and the company has confirmed that no further appearances or marketing appearances will be scheduled for him.
summary: The distributors of an upcoming Australian film based on a book by David Walliams said he will be removed from the movie. Transmission Films confirmed he will also not participate in the film’s media campaign before its 14 January cinema debut.
author: Guardian World

title: California Democrats ask Trump admin about detained 8‑year‑old Haitian boy in San Diego
content:
Democratic lawmakers in California are pressing the Trump administration for information about an eight‑year‑old Haitian boy who was placed in restraints and taken into federal immigration custody after arriving for an immigration check‑in in San Diego. The officials say the child was led away by three armed officers following a routine appointment, according to a video obtained by NBC News.

The lawmakers are seeking answers regarding the boy’s safety and current location, noting that the incident occurred on 4 November when the family said the check‑in was a standard immigration appointment. The request for clarification comes after the video showed the third‑grader being escorted by the officers.
summary: California Democrats ask Trump admin about detained 8‑year‑old Haitian boy in San Diego.
author: Guardian World

title: Ecuadorian journalist Tomás Beltrán shot dead while parking his car amid gang violence
content:
Tomás Beltrán was shot dead while maneuvering his car into his garage on Sunday night. The Ecuadorian journalist had run a Facebook page that reported news about Calceta, a small city in the province of Manabí.

Beltrán’s killing occurred amid gang warfare that has turned Ecuador into one of Latin America’s most violent countries. Calceta’s Pacific coastline makes it a key flashpoint in the gang conflict over drug‑trafficking routes.
summary: Tomás Beltrán, an Ecuadorian journalist who ran a Facebook page about Calceta in Manabí, was shot dead while manoeuvring his car into his garage on Sunday night. The killing occurred amid gang warfare over drug‑trafficking routes that has turned Ecuador into one of Latin America’s most violent countries.
author: Guardian World

title: Argentinian lawyer Marcelo Kohen mocks UK historic sovereignty claim over Falklands waters
content: Argentinian lawyer Marcelo Kohen, who is representing Argentina at an international tribunal in Hamburg, criticized the United Kingdom’s claim that the British Crown holds historic sovereignty over parts of the oceans surrounding the Falkland Islands. Kohen said Britain is wrong to rely on a “historic doctrine” that treats those waters as a Dominium maris Britannici, likening the approach to a 17th‑century colonial power. Argentina told the tribunal that the UK should not be permitted to act on that doctrine in the ongoing Falklands oil case.
summary: Marcelo Kohen, an Argentine lawyer representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked the United Kingdom’s claim that the British crown holds historic sovereignty over waters around the Falkland Islands. He said Britain should not act as a 17th‑century colonial power treating those waters as a Dominium maris Britannici.
author: Guardian World

title: Former Red Brigades member Leonardo Bertulazzi escapes house arrest in Argentina
content:
Leonardo Bertulazzi, a 74‑year‑old former member of Italy’s Red Brigades, escaped house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina, according to the country’s security ministry. The ministry said Bertulazzi hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork, used a harness and lowered himself from a fifth‑floor balcony.

Bertulazzi has been awaiting extradition to Italy, where he is slated to serve a 27‑year prison term imposed in 1987 for joining a subversive association and belonging to an armed group. Argentine authorities placed him under house arrest in 2024 pending the extradition.
summary: Former Red Brigades member Leonardo Bertulazzi escapes house arrest in Argentina.
author: Guardian World

title: Watch: Vinícius Jr's surprise message to boy who received prosthetic legs after Sudan drone strike
content: Real Madrid forward Vinícius Jr sent a surprise video message to 13‑year‑old fan Zaher, who lost both legs when a drone struck him in Khartoum in 2024. Zaher has since been fitted with prosthetic legs, and the player’s message was recorded to acknowledge the boy’s situation.
summary: Real Madrid player Vinícius Jr sent a surprise message to 13-year-old fan Zaher who lost both his legs after being hit by a drone in Khartoum, in 2024.
author: BBC World

title: 11-month-old baby found buried alive in crate near father's home in South Carolina
content: Officials in South Carolina said an 11‑month‑old baby who had been missing was discovered buried alive in a crate near his father’s home on Tuesday, a day after he was taken. The child is currently receiving care in a hospital.
summary: Officials said the missing 11-month-old baby was found buried alive in a crate close to his father's home on Tuesday. He was found a day after he was taken and is now being cared for in a hospital.
author: BBC World

title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona as thousands join Spain's housing and cost‑of‑living strike
content: Clashes broke out in Barcelona as thousands of demonstrators joined a Spain-wide general strike. The strike, organized by the country’s main unions, has drawn tens of thousands of participants and is focused on demands related to housing and the high cost of living.
summary: Clashes broke out in Barcelona as tens of thousands joined the general strike. The strike was called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
author: BBC World

title: The Rings of Power Season 3 Review: Revamp Too Little, Too Late
content: They’ve sidelined the harfoots, introduced a Stranger Things star and thrown in full-blooded romance. It’s probably not enough to stop the fantasy prequel feeling boring, though It might seem strange to characterise the leading streaming show from one of the most dominant corporations on the planet as a scrappy underdog. But after a lavish-but-dramatically stilted debut in 2022 and a similarly well-heeled but darker second season in 2024, it does feel like prequel series The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is somehow stuck on the back foot. For all its finely wrought art direction and respect for JRR Tolkien’s elaborate high-fantasy taxonomy, this no-expense-spared expansion of the mythos – set in the Second Age of Middle-earth, thousands of years before Bilbo Baggins first went walkabout – is in danger of going down in our own historical annals as simply a bit dull. Never mind more rings, it desperately needs some rizz.
summary: The third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power introduces a Stranger Things star and full-blooded romance while sidelining the harfoots. The review argues these changes are insufficient to prevent the fantasy prequel from feeling boring.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Gay Sauna Travelogue Challenges Central Europe’s Illiberal Image
content: A new book, With Wittgenstein in a Gay Sauna, reveals the deep-rooted queer subcultures in cities from Budapest to Prague – defying regional stereotypes and inspiring an art exhibition on masculinity The philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein argued that our understanding of reality is fundamentally bound by and shaped by the language we use to talk about it. But there is one place where the Vienna-born thinker’s argument ceases to make sense. “Gay saunas are spaces where language dies,” says Vratislav Maňák, a Czech writer and literary scholar. With Wittgenstein in a Gay Sauna, a book that made a major splash when it was published in Czech and German earlier this year, Maňák fictionalises Wittgenstein, who had romantic relations with both men and women, entering a Viennese Herrensauna called Kaiserbründl, hailed in newspapers at the time as “the most stylish bathing establishment in the world”.
summary: A new book reveals deep-rooted queer subcultures in cities from Budapest to Prague, defying regional stereotypes. The work also inspired an art exhibition on masculinity.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Rivals review: Second part of series two offers more than just comedy
content:
The second series of the television drama Rivals has been divided into two six-episode parts by Disney, a decision the reviewer attributes to the streaming company’s revenue-maximizing strategies. This review covers the second part of the series, which begins five months after the events of the first part. The narrative resumes with the funeral of Monica Campbell-Black, who died in a car accident during the Great Storm of 1987. Her death occurred after she discovered an affair between her husband, Tony, and Maud, the wife of Tony’s bitter enemy, and subsequently demanded a divorce.

The episode focuses on the interactions among the characters at the funeral, highlighting their romantic entanglements and rivalries. The reviewer notes significant tension and desire among the attendees, including Taggie and Rupert, who are described as yearning for each other across the aisle. Additionally, Freddie and Lizzie are depicted as being mutually attracted, with their physical features, such as Freddie’s moustache and Lizzie’s perm, noted as quivering in response to one another.

Further romantic dynamics are explored involving Gerald and Charles, who share a silent expression of love in a car after the service, particularly in the presence of Gerald’s new fiancée, Muffy. The review also mentions James, who is described as being transfixed by his own reflection. The article characterizes the show as containing moments of real poignancy alongside its usual themes of betrayal and romantic conflict, suggesting the series offers more depth than a simple romp.
summary: The second part of series two of Rivals features moments of real poignancy alongside its usual humor. The narrative resumes at the funeral of Monica, who died in a car crash after discovering Tony's affair.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jonathan Ross calls himself horrified by David Walliams and Russell Brand revelations
content: TV presenter says he was ‘genuinely unaware’ of pair’s conduct despite joking about Walliams going home with 15-year-old girl in 2004 Read the full investigation: ‘It wasn’t long until he asked me if I’d ever had sex before’ Explainer: the key legal issues surrounding the case The TV presenter Jonathan Ross has said he is “as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation”, adding that he was “genuinely unaware of their conduct” despite making a joke about a 15-year-old “going home” with Walliams at the British Comedy Awards in 2004. Walliams, one of Britain’s best-known television personalities and top-selling children’s authors, has been accused by several women of using his power and celebrity status to prey on young women and teenagers for sex.
summary: TV presenter Jonathan Ross said he was “as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation”. He added that he was “genuinely unaware of their conduct” despite making a joke about a 15‑year‑old girl going home with Walliams at the 2004 British Comedy Awards.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jane Wiedlin on new memoir TMI and Go-Go’s historic No.1 album record
content: As she releases a brutally honest memoir, the new wave icon opens up about industry sexism, living with bipolar disorder and becoming ‘the world’s first atheist ordained minister’ The first thing Jane Wiedlin tells me before our interview even begins is that, an hour or so earlier, she downed two beers. “It keeps me cheerful,” she says with a laugh. The disclosure dovetails with the reason we’re doing the interview in the first place, which is to unpack her new memoir, a tome that deserves a truth-in-advertising award for its title alone: TMI (as in “too much information”). “I’ve always been TMI!” Wiedlin proudly announces. “I’m the one who always wanted to expose the truth. This book is my first opportunity to do so.” A portion of that truth has to do with the band she helped form in the late 70s, the Go-Go’s. The five-piece are not only the first all-female band who play their own instruments and write their own material to earn a No 1 album in the US but, astonishingly, are the only such group to hold that distinction nearly 45 years later. The group’s power-pop music, heard in zippy hits like Our Lips Are Sealed and Vacation, led to their induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021, inspired a Broadway play and influenced modern female artists all the way from Olivia Rodrigo to Wet Leg.
summary: Jane Wiedlin on new memoir TMI and Go-Go’s historic No.1 album record.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Walliams loses legal bid to stay anonymous after ITV and Guardian name him
content: Rowan Atkinson, 55, was identified in reports by ITV News and the Guardian on Tuesday. The disclosure followed his unsuccessful court bid to prevent the public release of allegations against him.
summary: The 55-year-old failed in a court bid to stop allegations from being made public. He was subsequently named in reports by ITV News and the Guardian on Tuesday.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Tatum, Celtics beat 76ers 123-101 as Brown scores 13 in return to Boston
content:
The Boston Celtics defeated the Philadelphia 76ers 123-101 on Tuesday night, with Jayson Tatum scoring 21 points and Paul George adding 36 in his return to Philadelphia. Tatum outplayed his former teammate, Jaylen Brown, who struggled in his first game against Boston since being traded to the Sixers over the summer. Brown recorded 13 points and four turnovers while dealing with early foul trouble.

The matchup drew significant attention due to the intense scrutiny surrounding the players' relationship. Tatum appeared to ignore Brown before the game, and both athletes have refused to discuss their frosty dynamic. This head-to-head contest was considered one of the more anticipated early-season matchups.
summary: Jayson Tatum scored 21 points while Paul George added 36 in the Celtics' 123-101 victory over the 76ers. Jaylen Brown recorded 13 points and four turnovers in his first game against Boston since being traded to Philadelphia.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Harry Kane's diet changes and health regime aid record England cap
content:
Harry Kane is set to earn his 126th international cap for England on Thursday, a milestone attributed to his obsessive attention to detail and rigorous health regime. The striker recently revealed that he previously indulged in sweets, such as Haribo, after matches, a habit he described as a personal reward following intense 90-minute efforts.

Kane decided to eliminate these treats at the beginning of last season. He noted that after making this change, he felt sharper and capable of sprinting more frequently and executing a greater number of accelerations. While the article questions whether this specific dietary adjustment or his broader, extensive health routine is responsible for his improved performance, it highlights his commitment to physical optimization.

This dedication to his well-being is part of a broader strategy that includes other measures, such as consuming bone broth and undergoing acupuncture, as detailed in the article’s title. These practices are cited as key factors in helping the England captain reach new heights in his career and continue his record-breaking run of appearances for the national team.
summary: Harry Kane has eliminated sweets from his diet as part of a broader health regime that includes bone broth and acupuncture. These obsessive attention to detail measures are helping the striker reach a record 126th international appearance.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jacob Bethell battles fitness for South Africa Tests after knee surgery
content:
Jacob Bethell is battling to be fit for England’s Test series in South Africa, which begins on 17 December, after being ruled out of the white-ball tour of Australia. The 23-year-old all-rounder was sent back to the UK with swelling on his knee following surgery on his right knee at the end of August.

While Bethell was not expected to be ready for the one-day internationals starting in Perth on Friday, it was initially hoped he would feature in the subsequent Twenty20 matches.
summary: Jacob Bethell battles fitness for South Africa Tests after knee surgery.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Dennis Breakwell, Somerset and Northamptonshire cricketer, dies aged 78
content:
Dennis Breakwell, a left-arm spinner who played for Northamptonshire and Somerset, has died at the age of 78. His 15-year professional career included playing alongside notable cricketers such as Ian Botham and Viv Richards during the county’s glory days. Following his playing career, Breakwell spent more than 20 years working as a groundsman and coach at King’s College Taunton.

At the school, Breakwell maintained a quiet presence, cutting the grass and observing the game while serving as a mentor to young players. He is remembered for passing on his experience to generations of cricketers who passed through the institution, including Jos Buttler. The article, an extract from The Guardian’s weekly cricket email, The Spin, describes him as a stalwart who embodied the traditional, welcoming nature of the sport away from television coverage.
summary: Left-arm spinner Dennis Breakwell has died at the age of 78 following a 15-year career with Northamptonshire and Somerset. He also served for more than 20 years as a groundsman and coach at King’s College Taunton, where he mentored players including Jos Buttler.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bilic urges Croatia to use 7-0 loss as fuel for Wembley rematch against England
content:
Croatia prepares to face England at Wembley on Thursday in the Nations League, aiming to use the 7-0 defeat suffered by the same opponents just over a month ago as fuel. Manager Slaven Bilic stated that the home humiliation has left a scar on Croatian football, but he wants the team to harness that experience for a positive effect in the rematch.

Despite the fresh wounds and lingering unease, Bilic maintains his belief in ambitious goals. However, the article notes an unspoken impression that Croatia might be satisfied to accept another defeat if it is gentle by score and hard-fought by approach. In this context, the match is viewed less as a contest for points and more as an opportunity for the team to regain its self-respect.
summary: Croatia manager Slaven Bilic wants the team to turn their recent 7-0 defeat by England into motivation for their upcoming Nations League match at Wembley. The article notes that while Croatia views the previous loss as a humiliation, they may accept a gentle defeat in this rematch to regain self-respect.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Danny Kelly, football broadcaster and renowned editor, dies aged 69
content: Danny Baker pays tribute to the ‘funniest man I knew’ Kelly was former editor of the NME and Q magazines The journalist and broadcaster Danny Kelly, who helped define coverage of music and football in the UK for a generation, has died at the age of 69. Kelly edited the NME and Q Magazine and launched the Football 365 website before going on to be a presenter and pundit on the BBC and TalkSport. He had been receiving treatment for oesophageal cancer.
summary: Danny Kelly, former editor of the NME and Q Magazine and football broadcaster, died at age 69. He launched the Football 365 website, worked as a presenter and pundit on the BBC and TalkSport, and had been receiving treatment for oesophageal cancer.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United close on Mauricio Pochettino deal before settling Carrick’s fate
content:
Manchester United are preparing for a board meeting on Wednesday as the club moves closer to a potential appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as head coach. The former Paris Saint‑Germain manager, who currently leads the United States men’s national team, has expressed a desire to leave his USA role for the United job.

The club is reportedly in the final stages of agreeing a deal with Pochettino, contingent on the dismissal of Michael Carrick. This move follows recommendations from Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, and Omar Berrada, chief executive, to Sir Jim Ratcliffe. If Carrick is sacked, Pochettino is expected to take over the managerial position.
summary: Manchester United close on Mauricio Pochettino deal before settling Carrick’s fate.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bethell out of Australia trip and doubt for SA
content:
Jacob Bethell is ruled out of England’s white‑ball tour of Australia.  

He is a huge doubt for the Test tour of South Africa following the recurrence of a knee injury.
summary: Jacob Bethell is ruled out of England’s white-ball tour of Australia and is a huge doubt for the Test tour of South Africa following the recurrence of a knee injury.
author: BBC Sport

title: Rep. Ralph Norman grades President Trump ‘F’ on South Carolina midterms after primary loss
content: Rep. Ralph Norman (R‑S.C.) gave President Trump a failing grade for his performance in South Carolina’s midterm elections. Norman explained that a Trump‑backed Senate candidate defeated him in the Republican primary, only for that candidate to lose to a Democrat in the general election. He made the comment to MeidasTouch on Tuesday.
summary: Rep. Ralph Norman grades President Trump ‘F’ on South Carolina midterms after primary loss.

title: Democrats and Republicans unite to investigate Nvidia over alleged security breach
content: Republicans and Democrats have united in calling for investigations into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Lawmakers are examining whether this relationship compromised U.S. national security, with inquiries spanning intelligence, foreign relations, and banking committees. However, the two parties diverge on whether President Trump is at fault.
summary: Republicans and Democrats are showing rare unity in their calls for investigations into whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang compromised U. S.

title: House Republicans name Rep. Jim Jordan to lead diminished conference
content: House Republicans selected Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) to lead their conference in the next Congress. The party, described as diminished and battered by midterm results, is betting that Jordan, a conservative figure and former leadership opponent, can restore their competitive edge and help them find a path back to power.
summary: House Republicans chose Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) to lead the party's diminished conference in the next Congress. They hope his conservative style will help the party recover after the midterm losses.

title: 2026 Midterms End Israel’s Influence Over American Politics
content: The 2026 midterms have concluded Israel’s influence over American politics, according to the provided text. Opposing AIPAC’s agenda has evolved into a moral litmus test for elections, a distinction the source claims few other issues possess.

content: NPR's Steve Inskeep spoke with former CIA analyst Emily Harding regarding China's espionage tactics. The discussion centered on the alleged plot targeting the CEO of Nvidia.
summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep interviewed former CIA analyst Emily Harding. They discussed China's spy tactics related to an alleged plot targeting Nvidia's CEO.

title: Ohio's Jim Jordan to lead House Republicans in new Congress
content: Ohio Representative Jim Jordan, a close ally of President Trump and co-founder of the Freedom Caucus, will lead House Republicans when the new Congress begins in January.

title: Iran-backed trio accused of plotting attacks on U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
content: Iran-backed operatives have been charged with plotting nearly 20 attacks, including a scheme targeting a U.K. base that houses U.S. troops. In a separate matter, a U.S. soldier is currently detained in the U.K. on allegations of spying for Russia.
summary: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U. K.

title: House effectively ends Hegseth impeachment. And, 3 men accused of plotting U.K. attacks
content: The House has effectively ended its impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, sparing him from the proceedings for the time being. In a separate development, federal prosecutors arrested three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives who plotted attacks in the U.K.

title: Back of the net! Scotland’s historic salmon fishers – in pictures
content:
Colin McPherson has devoted three decades to the project “Catching the Tide,” a moving portrayal of fishers and an old way of life that is dying out.  

The series captures Scotland’s historic salmon fishers, offering a visual record of a tradition that is fading.
summary: Back of the net! Scotland’s historic salmon fishers – in pictures.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Britain's polluted streets persist as car industry resists electric vehicle shift
content:
George Monbiot, a Guardian columnist, argues that Britain’s streets remain polluted because the car industry resists change while politicians allow it to proceed. He contends that the transition to electric vehicles (EVs) is not moving as quickly as it should due to industry incompetence, expedience, and political cowardice. Monbiot describes a pattern where industries lobby governments, mobilize media, and fund think tanks to delay necessary shifts, often citing threats to jobs or the national interest, though he suggests their primary concern is the cost of retooling plants or developing new protocols.

The columnist notes that this dynamic, which he says triggered the Dutch nitrate crisis and UK exemptions from pesticide bans, is now driving the UK’s EV transition crisis. As the global climate summit, Cop31, begins, Monbiot states that the UK faces a major, predictable, and avoidable increase in greenhouse gas emissions. He attributes this outcome to the industry’s resistance and the government’s failure to enforce timely changes, resulting in continued pollution despite the availability of electric vehicle technology.
summary: The transition to electric vehicles should be moving apace, but it is not. And why?
author: Guardian Environment

title: H5N1 Bird Flu Kills Over 53,000 Female Elephant Seals on South Georgia
content:
The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) is preparing to update its Red List of endangered species, noting that determining the full impact of a pandemic remains difficult. In 2023, brown skuas arrived on South Georgia’s sub‑Antarctic island carrying the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1. Within months, the island’s southern elephant seals, which had come ashore to breed, fell ill. Mothers and newborn pups appeared weak, trembling, and many struggled to breathe.

The outbreak triggered a catastrophic die‑off. By 2025, more than 53,000 female elephant seals had died on South Georgia, a loss that is especially alarming because the island hosts over half of the global breeding population. The event underscores the severe consequences of bird flu on marine mammal populations and raises concerns about potential future extinctions.
summary: Scientists report that the H5N1 avian influenza outbreak on South Georgia killed more than 53,000 female elephant seals by 2025. Scientists say the island hosts more than half of the global breeding population, raising concerns about extinction risks.
author: Guardian Environment

title: UK foreign secretary warns climate crisis threatens national security of all countries
content:
Ed Miliband, the UK’s foreign secretary, will warn world leaders at COP31 in Turkey that the national security of all countries is at risk from the climate crisis. He says “science fiction” scenarios of widespread destruction are now regular occurrences and economic shocks from fossil fuels are now the norm.

He will address COP31 on Wednesday, stating that security and defence objectives are the new frontier of climate action because rapid heating will lead to food shortages, widespread economic disruption, migration and conflict.
summary: The UK’s foreign secretary warned that the climate crisis puts the national security of every country at risk. At the Cop31 summit in Turkey, Ed Miliband said that rapid heating will cause food shortages, economic disruption, migration and conflict, making security and defence the new frontier of climate action.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Study identifies potential strategy to reduce breast reconstruction complications after proton therapy
content: A study has identified a potential strategy to reduce breast reconstruction complications following proton therapy. Radiation therapy is sometimes required after mastectomy and breast reconstruction for breast cancer, but patients with implant-based reconstructions face a higher risk of capsular contracture. This complication involves scar tissue tightening around the implant, which can lead to pain, firmness, or distortion and may necessitate additional surgery.
summary: Radiation therapy is sometimes needed after mastectomy and breast reconstruction for breast cancer. However, patients with implant-based reconstruction who receive radiation therapy have a higher risk of capsular contracture, a complication in which scar tissue tightens around the implant.
author: Medical Xpress

title: FIU engineers create portable device to detect preterm birth risk
content:
Biomedical engineers at Florida International University have built a portable imaging device called PPRIM (Portable Preterm Imaging) that can detect early signs of preterm labor risk in about five seconds.  

The system could flag risk up to three months earlier than current screening methods.
summary: Biomedical engineers at Florida International University built a portable imaging device called PPRIM that can detect early signs of preterm labor risk in about five seconds. The system could flag risk up to three months earlier than current screening methods.

title: Children traveling over 60 miles for surgery face higher complications and longer stays
content:
A recent study published in the Journal of the American College of Surgeons found that nearly one in eight children undergoing a common inpatient surgical procedure lived more than 60 miles (97 kilometers) from the hospital where they were treated.  

Those children had higher odds of complications, longer hospital stays, and higher hospital charges compared with children who lived closer to the hospital.
summary: Children traveling over 60 miles for surgery face higher complications and longer stays.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Few Eligible Teens Receive New Obesity Treatments
content: A new study from Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago, published in JAMA Pediatrics, reports that most teens eligible for weight‑loss treatment receive neither powerful new anti‑obesity medications nor surgery, despite growing evidence supporting both options.
summary: A study from Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago found that most eligible teens are not receiving powerful new anti‑obesity medications or weight‑loss surgery. The study was published in JAMA Pediatrics.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Millions of Americans face huge challenges in long‑term care
content:
For millions of Americans, long‑term care creates huge financial, logistical and emotional difficulties.  

Private long‑term care insurance is prohibitively expensive or unavailable, and most older Americans are not eligible for Medicaid until they have depleted nearly all of their financial resources.
summary: Millions of Americans struggle with financial, logistical, and emotional challenges in long‑term care. Private long‑term care insurance is prohibitively expensive or simply unavailable, and most older Americans aren't eligible for Medicaid until they exhaust nearly all their financial resources.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Stress linked to lower quality of life for adults with multiple chronic conditions
content: A new study from the University of Eastern Finland reports that perceived stress is more strongly associated with poorer health‑related quality of life in adults who have two or more chronic conditions than in adults without chronic conditions.
summary: Perceived stress is more strongly associated with poorer health‑related quality of life among adults living with two or more chronic conditions than among those without chronic conditions. The finding comes from a new study conducted by the University of Eastern Finland.

content: The article highlights that neighborhoods play a crucial role in supporting healthy aging, a central concern for aging societies. It notes that, despite this importance, little is known about how dog walking—a routine activity—interacts with the neighborhood environment in dense Asian cities.
summary: The study examines how neighborhoods support healthy aging in aging societies. It notes that little is known about how dog walking interacts with the neighborhood environment in dense Asian cities, where health effects of dog ownership differ by location.

title: Common skin cancer rates rise faster in women, study finds
content:
New research led by QIMR Berghofer has uncovered a decades‑long increase in the rates of a common form of skin cancer across Australia and Europe.  

The study highlights a growing but under‑recognized public health challenge, noting that the rise is faster in women.
summary: Research led by QIMR Berghofer found a decades-long increase in the rates of a common form of skin cancer across Australia and Europe. The study highlights a growing but underrecognized public health challenge.

content: Measles is surging in the U. S., and a new tool developed by Johns Hopkins researchers estimates that the 2025 outbreak carried an economic cost of more than $37 million.
summary: A new tool developed by Johns Hopkins researchers estimates that the 2025 measles outbreak in the U. S.

content: New research from Murdoch University has revealed that Carnaby's cockatoos depend on small, fragmented patches of native vegetation to survive in heavily cleared landscapes—a finding that could play an important role in protecting the endangered species.
summary: The study found that Carnaby's cockatoos depend on small, fragmented patches of native vegetation to survive in heavily cleared landscapes. The findings could help protect the endangered species.

content: Around 1,800 years ago, an Iron Age/Roman gully near Cambridge contained more than 9,000 bones, most of them from frogs. When archaeologists excavated the site, they speculated whether the remains were the result of a Roman frog feast or the skeletal aftermath of a ritual.
summary: Archaeologists found over 9,000 bones, mainly frogs, in an Iron Age/Roman gully near Cambridge, about 1,800 years ago. Bone analysis suggests the remains were caused by owls, raising questions about whether the site was a Roman frog feast or a ritual.

content: A research group led by Yu Tao from the Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics (CIOMP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has proposed a new analytical phase readout algorithm for deep frequency modulation interferometry (DFMI). title: Wits University researchers reveal magneto‑optic effect in ordinary glass fiber
content:
For more than five decades, engineers have described light in optical fiber using a convenient shortcut that has rarely been questioned. The shortcut has been widely accepted as accurate for practical purposes.

A team of engineers at the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits University) in Johannesburg, South Africa, has now demonstrated that this shortcut conceals a small but real effect. They found that placing a magnet beside a multimode fiber—rather than along its length—can alter the light traveling inside the fiber.
summary: Wits University researchers reveal magneto‑optic effect in ordinary glass fiber.
author: Phys.org

title: Aluminum gallium nitride device detects nanowatt light and stores data up to 300 °C
content: Researchers reported in Nature Materials that a new aluminum gallium nitride device merges light detection, memory, and basic processing by controlling charge at polarization interfaces. The device can sense light at nanowatt‑per‑square‑centimeter levels and remains stable at temperatures up to 300 °C.
summary: Researchers have developed an aluminum gallium nitride device that combines light detection, memory and basic processing by controlling charge at polarization interfaces. The device can detect light at the nanowatt‑per‑square‑centimeter level and operate stably at temperatures up to 300 °C.

title: Voyager 1, Earth's farthest spacecraft, reshapes planet knowledge after 50 years
content: Voyager 1, the most distant human‑made object, is now only one light day from Earth. The spacecraft has completed a 50‑year journey to the edge of the solar system. What it observed along the way has revolutionised our understanding of the planets and ourselves.
summary: Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth. What it saw on its 50-year journey to the edge of the solar system revolutionised our understanding of the planets and ourselves.

title: University of Ottawa model proposes Universe is 26.7B years old, no dark matter needed
content:
A provocative new cosmological model proposes that the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old, roughly twice the age currently accepted. The theory also suggests that dark matter and dark energy might not be necessary to explain the Universe’s behavior.

Researchers from the University of Ottawa tested the model against several major astronomical observations. Their analysis indicated that the model could account for galaxy rotation, cosmic expansion, and the formation of early elements.
summary: University of Ottawa model proposes Universe is 26.7B years old, no dark matter needed.

title: Scientists find 1834 British coin shows evidence of minting accident
content:
Scientists uncovered a 192‑year‑old mystery hidden in a mangled silver coin.  

Advanced 3D scans and microscopic analysis revealed unusual metal distortions, suggesting the coin was crushed under extreme pressure, possibly during its original production.
summary: A bizarrely deformed 1834 British silver coin found at a car boot sale may preserve evidence of a rare minting accident nearly 200 years ago. Advanced 3D scans and microscopic analysis revealed unusual metal distortions suggesting the coin was crushed under extreme pressure, potentially during its original production.

title: Study Finds Overweight or Obese Dementia Patients Have Lower Risk of Death
content: A recent study involving more than 4,500 older adults found that individuals who were overweight or obese at the time of a dementia diagnosis had a 16 % to 27 % lower risk of death compared with those who were of normal weight. The research suggests that the additional energy and muscle reserves associated with higher body weight may help patients withstand the physical toll of dementia. However, the precise reason for this survival advantage remains unclear.
summary: A study of more than 4,500 older adults found that overweight or obese dementia patients had a 16% to 27% lower risk of death than normal-weight patients. Researchers suspect that extra energy and muscle reserves may help patients survive, but the reason for the survival advantage remains unclear.

content: Scientists have reported that the complex patterns of mammalian hair follicles can emerge from a simple mechanism in which cells respond to chemical signals. The new findings dispute a previously held theory and show that intricate biological designs can develop without a detailed pre‑existing blueprint.
summary: Scientists have discovered that the intricate patterns of hair follicles on mammals may arise from a simple process in which cells follow chemical signals. The findings challenge a long‑standing theory and show that complex biological patterns can form without a detailed blueprint.

title: Occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke, study finds
content: A study of more than 440,000 Americans found that cannabis use is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, and that occasional users have 40 % higher odds of reporting a history of stroke. Researchers note the findings raise concern about infrequent marijuana use, but they have not proven that cannabis directly causes strokes or heart disease.
summary: New research involving more than 440,000 Americans found cannabis use associated with increased cardiovascular risk, with occasional users showing 40% higher odds of reporting a history of stroke. Researchers note the findings raise concern about infrequent use but have not established that cannabis directly causes strokes or heart disease.
author: Science Daily

title: Energy drinks linked to 11‑fold rise in cardiac arrest reports
content:
A recent study reports a significant association between energy drinks and stimulant supplements and serious heart problems. The analysis found 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest and 4.5 times more reports of heart attacks linked to these products compared with other substances.

Nearly half of the cardiovascular reports involving energy drinks and stimulants involved young adults, prompting concerns about the potential risks of these products. The study, however, could not establish a causal relationship, noting that the findings only indicate a strong correlation.
summary: A new study found energy drinks and stimulant supplements were associated with 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest and 4.5 times more reports of heart attacks. Young adults accounted for nearly half of the cardiovascular reports involving these products, though the study could not prove causation.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA reports Antarctic ozone hole expands to seventh‑largest size in 2026
content: NASA reported that the Antarctic ozone hole reached its seventh‑largest size on record in 2026, the biggest extent not seen in a decade. Unusual weather conditions pushed the hole near its historic maximum, but scientists noted that international restrictions on ozone‑depleting chemicals limited further damage, and the ozone layer continues to recover.
summary: The Antarctic ozone hole expanded to its seventh‑largest size on record in 2026. Scientists said international restrictions on ozone‑destroying chemicals prevented greater damage and that Earth's ozone layer is still recovering.
author: Science Daily

title: Homo naledi site in South Africa shows all-female burial of 20 individuals
content: A study of a South African cave burial indicates that an extinct human relative may have assembled an all‑female site more than 240,000 years ago. Researchers examined ancient proteins preserved in the teeth of Homo naledi specimens and detected no male‑specific markers among at least 20 individuals, a finding that could resolve a decade‑long mystery.
summary: Scientists examined ancient proteins in Homo naledi teeth from a South African cave and identified no male-specific markers among at least 20 individuals. The findings suggest the burial site, dated to more than 240,000 years ago, may have been composed entirely of females.
author: Science Daily

title: Blood molecular signal may flag early changes preceding ovarian cancer
content: Researchers reported that a molecular signal detectable in blood can identify microscopic changes that occur before ovarian cancer develops, representing a potential diagnostic breakthrough for a disease that is often discovered after it has already spread. The finding was detailed in a report published on Tuesday in Nature Medicine. The authors noted that for decades, efforts to detect ovarian cancer earlier have centered on locating smaller tumors, highlighting the significance of a blood‑based marker for earlier risk assessment.
summary: Researchers discovered a molecular signal in blood that identifies microscopic changes that precede ovarian cancer, offering a potential diagnostic breakthrough for a disease often discovered after it has spread. The findings were reported in a study published on Tuesday in Nature Medicine.
author: Guardian Science

title: Navajo Reservoir rises nearly 60 ft, reaching 108% capacity, its highest level since 2019
content:
Heavy rainstorms that swept the Four Corners region in late October and early November 2026 caused a rapid rise in the water level of Navajo Reservoir. Satellite images taken with the Operational Land Imager on Landsat 9 show the lake on September 20 and again on November 7, illustrating a rise of almost 60 feet (18 meters) during that period, according to data from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. On November 7 the reservoir reached its highest level since August 2019 and held 108 percent of the average capacity for that date, a sharp contrast to the 60 percent of average capacity recorded on September 20.

The surge followed back‑to‑back extreme rain events that produced precipitation totals two to four times the regional average from early September through early November. While the downpours provided short‑term relief to a Southwest already suffering from long‑term drought and a winter‑time snow drought, they also pushed river levels to record or near‑record heights. The San Juan, Piedra and other rivers swelled, and the town of Pagosa Springs, Colorado—about 40 miles northeast of the reservoir—experienced severe flooding. The first rain event deposited 5.05 inches (12.8 cm) in Pagosa Springs, and the San Juan River reached major flood stage on October 23. A second surge on November 1 brought the river close to the 1911 record level, prompting evacuation orders and rescues of dozens of people as water inundated streets and damaged property.

The heavy rainfall also altered reservoir management. The Bureau of Reclamation reduced releases from Navajo Dam on September 16 and 17, a change noted alongside the observed rise in lake level. Because the spring melt was limited by snow drought, the reservoir had seen little growth earlier in the year, making the autumn inflows a dominant factor in its rapid filling.

Weekly U.S. Drought Monitor maps, which combine satellite data and ground observations, recorded an improvement in short‑term drought conditions across the Southwest and Great Basin after the storms, although long‑term drought persisted in some areas. Experts linked the unusual low‑latitude storm that delivered the autumn rains to an ongoing El Niño, which can steer moisture‑laden systems into the interior Southwest.

The story, written by Lindsey Doermann and illustrated with NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, draws on several sources, including AP News, the Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes, The Gazette, NOAA’s National Water Prediction Service, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the U.S. Drought Monitor, and Weather West.
summary: Navajo Reservoir rises nearly 60 ft, reaching 108% capacity, its highest level since 2019.
author: NASA News

title: APOD shows dwarf galaxy NGC 4449 and its role in spreading heavy elements
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 11, 2026 features a Hubble Space Telescope image of the dwarf galaxy NGC 4449. The accompanying explanation notes that dwarf galaxies are roughly one‑tenth the size of the Milky Way, which spans about 100,000 light‑years, and that they contain only a few billion stars. Despite their modest scale, dwarf galaxies are described as the most common type of galaxy in the universe.

The entry highlights that NGC 4449 and similar dwarf galaxies are missing more oxygen than theoretical models predict. This discrepancy suggests that stellar winds and supernovae in these small systems are surprisingly effective at expelling oxygen and other heavy elements. The explanation proposes that such dwarf galaxies may therefore play a significant role in distributing heavy elements—the building blocks of stars, planets, and life—throughout the cosmos.

The image credit is given to NASA, ESA, A. Aloisi (STScI/ESA), and the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)‑ESA/Hubble Collaboration. The APOD entry lists Keighley Rockcliffe, Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, and Cecilia Chirenti as authors and editors. The service is provided by ASD at NASA GSFC, NASA Science Activation, and Michigan Tech. U.
summary: The November 11, 2026 Astronomy Picture of the Day features a Hubble image of dwarf galaxy NGC 4449. The explanation notes that NGC 4449 and similar dwarf galaxies lack expected oxygen, indicating their stellar winds and supernovae efficiently disperse heavy elements across the universe.
author: NASA News

title: Black Ops II statically recompiled to native ARM64 macOS runs at ~60fps
content: I grew up with Black Ops 2 and wanted to see if I could make it work on my 2020 MacBook Pro. So I used Claude Opus 5.5 to create a tool that converts your copy of the game (from Steam) to a native ARM64 Mac app, with almost 60fps in all areas. The whole game is statically recompilated ahead-of-time (AOT) and does not use any emulator whatsoever, be it Wine, Crossover or Rosetta. The best thing is the performance, although some heat issues are still to fix. You get to play the whole Campaign, local Multiplayer (with bots) and local Zombies (all DLCs maps; you need to have them in your Steam library obviously) at about 60fps. Split-screen was not in the PC version, but I've been working on it lately; it's coming soon! LAN mode is on the roadmap for later too :) Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50449891 Points: 61 # Comments: 22
summary: I grew up with Black Ops 2 and wanted to see if I could make it work on my 2020 MacBook Pro. So I used Claude Opus 5.5 to create a tool that converts your copy of the game (from Steam) to a native ARM64 Mac app, with almost 60fps in all areas.
