title: Tech Review explores mind preservation ideas and warns of open AI model risks
content: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind As we age, we forget most of what we’ve experienced, yet there’s still undeniable continuity: At 30, or 50, or 70, you will still be you. To preserve that elusive continuity of self, some far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to keep the brain going, even beyond death. Their ideas range from freezing brains in liquid nitrogen to augmenting living ones and uploading our memories to the cloud. Here are six possible paths for keeping your mind going, and how feasible they might be. —Antonio Regalado This story is from the Impossible edition of our print magazine. Subscribe now to get every issue as soon as it lands. MIT Technology Review Narrated: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks? Anthropic recently released a report arguing that a powerful new model released by the Chinese company Z. Ai, poses a major cyberattack risk. Its core concern was that it is freely available for anyone to download and modify. The warning was the latest flashpoint in the debate over open frontier AI models. Critics warn that bad actors can misuse them, while supporters argue they prevent a handful of companies from controlling the technology. The debate, however, is more complicated than it seems. This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 COP31’s flagship pledge to electrify 35% of energy use is sinking Only around a dozen nations are reportedly ready to sign it. ( Politico ) + It requires quadrupling the pace of electrification. ( New Scientist $) + John Kerry says the US must follow China on clean energy. ( Guardian ) + But the US skipped the talks entirely for a second year. ( NYT $) + What’s the future of electricity? ( MIT Technology Review ) 2 The Nvidia spy scandal reportedly involves $7.5 billion of chips Alice Huang allegedly obtained 240,000 restricted chips. ( Information $) + Trump was told of Huang’s spy link on Air Force One. ( NYT $) + Experts warn the scandal could erode America’s AI lead. ( Verge ) + Nvidia’s slide has let Microsoft overtake it in value. ( Reuters $) 3 Studies found AI agents go rogue because they’re “incorrigible” Their training rewards them for finishing tasks at any cost. ( NYT $) + This is why AI agents lie and cheat to reach their goals. ( MIT Technology Review ) 4 Anthropic has scaled back its IPO valuation to $1.4 trillion It aimed for $2 trillion before the recent AI jitters. ( Guardian ) 5 Drone strikes have wiped out 3% of Yandex’s cloud customer data Ukraine hit three of its data centers in October. ( Reuters $) + Ukraine’s drones are fighting data centers for fiber. ( Ars Technica ) 6 Moderna says its new vaccine could prevent cancer in high-risk people The company’s CEO calls it the “holy grail” of cancer prevention. ( FT $) + Hong Kong is testing a next-gen ultrasound cancer treatment. ( SCMP ) 7 Scientists have slowly reversed human cells’ ages by decades One age marker was set back as far as 60 years. ( Wired $) + “Reprogramming” is the buzziest de-aging idea. ( MIT Technology Review ) 8 Robot vessels are hunting for mines in the Strait of Hormuz AI helps them spot mines camouflaged on the seabed. ( BBC ) 9 Life may have started inside a tiny bubble That’s the idea behind the “lipid first” origin theory. ( Quanta ) 10 As Voyager 1 reaches a light day from Earth, here’s what it’s taught us Its discoveries rewrote textbooks in real time. ( New Scientist $) Quote of the day “What a dereliction of duty. He’s supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends.” —Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, accuses President Donald Trump of ignoring warnings about the alleged relationship between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese spy. One more thing How refrigeration ruined fresh food Bananas may not be chilled in the grocery store, but they’re the ultimate refrigerated fruit. It’s only thanks to a network of thermal control that they’ve become a global commodity. And that salad bag on the shelf? It’s not just a bag but a highly engineered respiratory apparatus. According to Nicola Twilley—a contributor to The New Yorker and cohost of the podcast Gastropod—refrigeration has wrecked our food system. Thankfully, there are promising alternative preservation methods. Read the full story on her research. —Allison Arieff We can still have nice things A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.) + A whisky made like wine is wowing the spirits world. + Britain lost in the fog makes for hauntingly beautiful photos. + Chronophoto is a fiendishly addictive game that challenges you to date old photos to the year. + Dozens of saxophonists met up in New York to play the gloriously cheesy riff from George Michael’s “Careless Whisper.”
summary: The newsletter outlines six speculative methods for extending consciousness after death, ranging from brain freezing to memory uploading. Anthropic warned that a powerful open model from Chinese company Z. Ai poses a major cyberattack risk because it can be freely downloaded and modified.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: German researchers gradually reverse human cell ages by decades
content: Researchers in Germany have gradually reversed the ages of human cells by several decades. This incremental de‑aging enabled the scientists to monitor the rejuvenation process in a manner that earlier experiments on cell rejuvenation had not been able to achieve.
summary: Researchers in Germany gradually reversed human cells’ ages by decades. By doing so, they could track the de‑aging process in a way previous rejuvenation experiments could not.
author: Wired

title: 13-year-old used Gemini on school Chromebook to discuss suicide; not flagged for weeks
content: Parents allege that their 13‑year‑old daughter accessed the Gemini AI on a school Chromebook to discuss and plan suicide. According to the family, the school’s monitoring systems failed to flag the conversation for several weeks, alerting staff only when the situation was nearly critical.
summary: Parents say their 13-year-old daughter used the Gemini AI on a school Chromebook to plan her suicide. The school's monitoring systems did not flag the activity for weeks, discovering it only when it was nearly too late.
author: Wired

title: Michigan voters approve ban on utility election spending, utilities file lawsuit
content: Michigan voters approved a ballot measure that limits utilities’ ability to spend money on elections, a decision framed by concerns over rising electricity costs. In response, the utilities have filed a lawsuit, arguing that the restriction infringes on their freedom of speech.
summary: Michiganders voted for a ballot proposition to curb utilities' ability to spend on elections. Utilities responded by suing, saying the measure limits their freedom of speech.
author: Wired

title: EU Digital Fairness Act targets Duolingo, Strava and Ticketmaster
content: The European Union’s Digital Fairness Act, which targets “dark patterns” on online platforms, requires changes such as allowing users to turn off winning‑streak features and obligating influencers to disclose paid promotions. Under the same legislation, companies including Duolingo, Strava and Ticketmaster are now subject to the new rules.
summary: Duolingo, Strava and Ticketmaster are subject to the EU’s new Digital Fairness Act. The act allows users to turn off winning streaks and requires influencers to disclose paid promotions to curb dark‑pattern practices.
author: Wired

title: Apple to shut down Support Community forum on November 20, 2026
content:
Apple has placed its dedicated Support Community forum into read-only mode, signaling the end of the platform where users previously exchanged advice and troubleshooted product issues. A banner notice on the website announces that the community will permanently close on November 20, 2026.

The site will no longer accept new posts starting immediately. Apple directs users to other channels for trusted guidance and support as the forum winds down.
summary: The Apple Support Community forum has been placed in read‑only mode and will permanently close on November 20, 2026. The site will no longer accept new posts.
author: The Verge

title: Serve Robotics launches developer portal to open 2,000 sidewalk robots to anyone
content:
Serve Robotics announced that it will open its autonomous last‑mile delivery platform to a broader audience. The company is launching an AV Delivery Developer Portal that will let third‑party software engineers, independent businesses and autonomous AI agents access its fleet of roughly 2,000 sidewalk robots.

Through the portal, developers and small businesses will be able to use Serve’s software tools to dispatch robots directly, without needing to work with major food‑delivery services such as Uber Eats. The service is already operating in about 150 neighborhoods, and a delivery robot was photographed rolling down a pedestrian walkway in Miami.
summary: Serve Robotics is launching an AV Delivery Developer Portal that lets third‑party software engineers, independent businesses and autonomous AI agents access its fleet of 2,000 sidewalk delivery robots. The portal allows users in the company’s 150 neighborhoods to dispatch robots directly without using major food‑delivery platforms such as Uber Eats.
author: The Verge

title: Early iPhone Duo buyers request refunds after two weeks
content: An open-and-shut case. For most new relationships, two weeks probably isn't enough time to decide if you're ready for long-term commitment. But two weeks with a new phone? You probably know. The iPhone Duo launched just over two weeks ago, and that's been enough time for a subset of day-one buyers who aren't loving the phone to make a decision: It's time to end things. Also, they wanted their $2,000 back. This is to be expected, to an extent; the Duo just isn't a phone for everyone. It's an early adopter device - we called it "a messy, expensive good time" - and on top of that, the hinge appears to be suffering some first-gen growing pains. Despite all that, Appl …
summary: The iPhone Duo launched just over two weeks ago and some day‑one buyers say they are not loving the phone. Those buyers want their $2,000 purchase back, citing the device’s high price and hinge issues.
author: The Verge

title: Reporter asks TV manufacturers 17 questions on data collection practices
content:
The author has reached out to every TV manufacturer with a set of 17 yes‑or‑no questions aimed at uncovering how these devices collect and use data. The inquiry focuses on potential spying practices, from listening to voice commands to capturing what is shown on screen.

Many customers worry that TVs and streaming devices might record conversations, take screenshots of viewing habits, store sensitive personal information locally, and share data with cloud services. The author’s questions are designed to clarify whether such practices are in place.

According to the author, spying is not limited to a single brand; every TV company is implicated, not just LG. While some data collection is deemed necessary for product functionality, the author notes that not all collected information is essential and may include details users prefer to keep private.
summary: The author sent a set of 17 yes-or-no questions to every TV and streaming device manufacturer about how they gather and use information. The inquiry highlighted concerns that companies collect data beyond what is needed for product operation, potentially including voice recordings, screen captures, and cloud sharing of private details.
author: The Verge

title: Skydance CEO says Paramount Plus and HBO Max still lag behind YouTube
content:
At Skydance’s first employee town hall following its October acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, CEO David Ellison told staff that the company behind Paramount Plus and HBO Max was competing for viewers’ attention with some of the world’s largest technology firms. Earlier, Ellison highlighted a short‑form vertical‑video feed as “critical to our future” for keeping audiences engaged with Paramount programming.

During Skydance’s earnings call on Monday, Ellison identified YouTube as a key rival, noting that when the broadcast, cable and streaming assets of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery are combined, they still lag behind YouTube.
summary: At Skydance's first employee town hall after it acquired Warner Bros. Discovery in October, CEO David Ellison told staff that the company behind Paramount Plus and HBO Max was competing for people's attention with some of the world's biggest tech companies.
author: The Verge

title: England's Office for Students urges return to exams as AI hampers coursework assessment
content:
The Office for Students (OfS), England’s higher‑education regulator, has advised universities to revert to traditional exams and in‑person presentations for grading. The recommendation follows an investigation that found lecturers say artificial‑intelligence tools have made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework.

The regulator warned that the credibility of English university degrees is under threat because AI is being used widely in essays, dissertations and “open book” exams, with some students reporting peers boasting of undetected AI assistance.
summary: The Office for Students said universities in England should revert to traditional exams and in‑person presentations to grade students. It warned that widespread AI use in essays, dissertations and open‑book exams is threatening the credibility of English university degrees, with students reporting peers boasting of undetected AI use.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Germany bans Chinese-made drones from military bases over security concerns
content: Germany has prohibited the use of commercially available Chinese‑made drones on its military bases and training grounds, citing security concerns. The ban reflects broader Western military worries that Chinese technology could transmit sensitive information to Beijing.
summary: Germany has banned commercially available Chinese-made drones from its military bases and training grounds due to security concerns, according to reports. Western military forces have grown increasingly worried that Chinese-made technology could transmit sensitive information to Beijing.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Judge allows Trump defamation suit against BBC to proceed, cuts claim to $5bn
content: A second claim brought under a Florida consumer protection law was thrown out, halving the original $10bn lawsuit to $5bn, but the US president has still hailed the ruling as “A Huge Victory”.
summary: Judge allows Trump defamation suit against BBC to proceed, cuts claim to $5bn.
author: Euronews

title: Novaya Gazeta shutters Moscow office after eviction and censorship
content: Russia’s last openly critical newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, has closed its Moscow office. The paper said that security services and censors forced it to stop operating after they evicted it, shut down its donation system, blocked its printing, and revoked its media registration.
summary: Novaya Gazeta said security services and censors forced it to stop operating. The paper was evicted, its donation system shut down, printing blocked, and its media registration revoked.
author: Euronews

title: Protesters at Israel's Knesset call for new elections, oppose Arab lawmakers
content: Protesters gathered outside Israel’s parliament in Jerusalem, demanding new elections. They voiced opposition to the presence and role of Arab lawmakers in the Knesset.
summary: Demonstrators gathered outside Israel's parliament in Jerusalem. They called for new elections and opposed the presence and role of Arab lawmakers in the Knesset.
author: Euronews

title: EU to hold defence talks in Doha to boost security ties with Qatar and Gulf
content:
The European Union announced plans to hold defence talks in Doha aimed at strengthening security ties with Qatar and other Gulf states.  

EU Ambassador to Qatar Antonino Maggiore told Euronews that Europe intends to deepen defence cooperation with Qatar and Gulf countries, while also expanding political and economic collaboration across the region.
summary: EU Ambassador to Qatar Antonino Maggiore said Europe plans to strengthen defence cooperation with Qatar and the Gulf countries. He also said Europe aims to deepen political and economic cooperation with the region.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo to travel to Peru for emotional homecoming after Argentina visit
content: Pope Leo will conclude his 12‑day South America tour with a Wednesday visit to Argentina, where a final event is expected to draw millions. Afterward he will travel to Peru, where the country is preparing for what officials describe as an emotional homecoming for the first Peruvian citizen to lead the Catholic Church.
summary: Pope Leo will wrap up his visit to Argentina on Wednesday, concluding a 12‑day South America tour. He will then travel to Peru for an emotional homecoming as the first Peruvian citizen to lead the Catholic Church, with a final event expected to draw millions.
author: France 24

title: Republicans block impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in House
content: On Tuesday, Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives united to derail an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Washington, D.C., correspondent Fraser Jackson reports further details.
summary: Republicans in the US House of Representatives voted on Tuesday to derail an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The report was filed by correspondent Fraser Jackson in Washington, DC.
author: France 24

title: Aneto Glacier in Spanish Pyrenees Melting Rapidly, Expected to Disappear Within a Decade
content: Within a decade, the Aneto glacier—one of southern Europe’s largest and situated on the highest peak of the Spanish Pyrenees—is expected to disappear as it melts at a rapid rate. FRANCE 24’s Maude Petit‑Jové, Mathilde Lopinski and Sarah Morris report that the glacier’s loss is viewed as another sign of global warming and offers valuable study material for glaciologists.
summary: Aneto glacier on the highest peak of the Spanish Pyrenees is melting rapidly and is expected to disappear within a decade. The glacier's loss is cited as evidence of global warming and a valuable case for glaciologists, according to a report by Maude Petit-Jové, Mathilde Lopinski and Sarah Morris for FRANCE 24.
author: France 24

title: UNICEF head Catherine Russell backs global children's rights pact at Paris Peace Forum
content: More than 50 countries, 20 non-governmental and philanthropic organisations and a series of multinational companies are pledging this week to put children's rights at the heart of their policies and actions. A pact is being agreed upon at the Paris Peace Forum, where the rights of children are taking centre stage.
summary: More than 50 countries, 20 non-governmental and philanthropic organisations and a series of multinational companies are pledging this week to put children's rights at the heart of their policies and actions. A pact is being agreed upon at the Paris Peace Forum, where the rights of children are taking centre stage.
author: France 24

title: AI tools increase online harassment of Middle East women
content: Women in the Middle East experience an above‑average share of online harassment and violence. According to the source, the spread of AI‑enabled tools is intensifying that online violence against women in the region.
summary: Women in the Middle East already have to deal with an above‑average share of online harassment and violence. The proliferation of AI‑enabled tools is making it worse.
author: DW World

title: Iran labels Argentina's navy and air force as terrorist organizations
content: Iran announced that it now classifies Argentina’s navy and air force as “terrorist organizations.” Tehran added that Buenos Aires is responsible for further consequences.
summary: Iran says it now considers Argentina's navy and air force to be terrorist organizations. Tehran claimed Buenos Aires is responsible for further consequences.
author: DW World

title: Tundu Lissu sentenced to four years for incitement after treason trial in Tanzania
content: Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu avoided a possible death‑by‑hanging sentence in a treason trial and was instead sentenced to four years in prison for incitement to unrest. The verdict raises questions about the ability of dissident voices to be heard in Tanzania.
summary: Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu faced a treason trial that could have resulted in death by hanging. He was instead convicted of incitement to unrest and sentenced to four years in prison.
author: DW World

title: Kenyan mother in Saudi Arabia sentenced to 100 lashes for out‑of‑marriage birth
content: Rights groups condemn reported punishment of Kenyan migrant worker as an ‘act of violence’ A Kenyan mother in Saudi Arabia has reportedly been sentenced to 100 lashes after giving birth outside marriage. Under the Saudi sharia law system, sex outside marriage is a criminal offence. But it is women who are disproportionately targeted, say rights groups, which have condemned the punishment as an “act of violence”.
summary: A Kenyan mother in Saudi Arabia has been sentenced to 100 lashes after giving birth outside marriage. Rights groups have condemned the punishment as an act of violence, saying that sex outside marriage is a criminal offence under Saudi sharia law and women are disproportionately targeted.
author: Guardian World

title: NAZA documentary on Gaza killings becomes one of year’s most watched
content:
The award-winning documentary NAZA, directed by Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, has been viewed by over 1.5 million people since its global cinema release last month. The film details Israel’s surveillance of Palestinian civilians and its mass killing of civilians in Gaza. As of Friday, 6 November, the movie has reached a worldwide audience of 1,547,033 viewers.

This viewership makes NAZA one of the most-watched documentary films with a theatrical release in 2026. The achievement highlights the film’s significant impact within less than two months of its initial screening.
summary: NAZA documentary on Gaza killings becomes one of year’s most watched.
author: Guardian World

title: Belgian law allowing police home raids on refused asylum seekers criticised as “law of fear”
content:
Belgian MPs have approved a law that authorises police to forcibly enter homes in order to remove people whose asylum applications have been refused. The measure is part of a broader effort by the ruling right‑leaning coalition to increase expulsions of individuals who have been denied the right to stay in the country.

Rights groups have condemned the legislation, warning that it could lead to “ICE‑style” raids similar to those in the United States. Campaigners say the new powers create a “law of fear” and have sparked months of intense debate across Belgium over the proposed expulsions.
summary: Rights groups say the new law letting police forcibly enter homes to remove refused asylum seekers creates a “law of fear”. MPs approved the measure, prompting comparisons to ICE-style immigration raids in the United States.
author: Guardian World

title: Nissan cuts petrol car output in China as EV sales surge
content:
Nissan announced that it will cut back on petrol‑car manufacturing in China, citing a faster‑than‑expected shift to new‑energy vehicles and a harsh market environment. The Japanese automaker said accelerating sales of electric and hybrid models in the country, combined with a brutal price war, have prompted it to revise its China sales forecasts downward.

In response, Nissan plans to increase production of battery‑electric vehicles and plug‑in hybrids, the latter pairing a smaller battery with a petrol engine, while reducing output of conventional gasoline models.
summary: Nissan said the shift to new‑energy vehicles in China is happening faster than expected and it has lowered its sales forecast for the market. The company will reduce petrol‑car production and boost output of battery‑electric vehicles and plug‑in hybrids as electric and hybrid sales accelerate amid a price war.
author: Guardian World

title: US envoys to meet Putin in Moscow and Zelenskyy in Dublin after peace talks progress
content: US negotiators to meet Putin in Moscow, Zelenskyy in Dublin next Separately, I am also keeping an eye on Italy, with reports that several schools are being evacuated after receiving bomb threats by emails. According to Rai and Sky TG24, the email was signed by “Mikhail Andropov” – the same name used in several hoax bomb alarms against European flights last week.
summary: US negotiators will meet Putin in Moscow and Zelenskyy in Dublin on separate visits. In Italy, several schools were evacuated after receiving bomb‑threat emails signed “Mikhail Andropov”, a name previously used in hoax bomb alarms against European flights.
author: Guardian World

title: Property investor lending falls fastest on record, CBA mortgage stress hits 12‑year high
content:
New lending to property investors fell at its fastest pace on record during the three months to September, as landlords respond to higher taxes, falling property prices and rising interest rates. The slowdown reflects a shift in investor activity amid the broader housing market pressures.

In the same period, the Commonwealth Bank said the proportion of its customers struggling to repay their mortgages rose to a 12‑year high. The bank’s figures highlight growing repayment difficulties for Australian homeowners.
summary: New lending to property investors fell at its fastest pace on record through the three months to September as landlords faced higher taxes, falling property prices and rising interest rates. The Commonwealth Bank reported that the share of its customers struggling to repay mortgages had risen to a 12‑year high.
author: Guardian World

title: One Nation Victoria candidate apologises for slew of offensive comments about lesbians, Indians and Julia Gillard
content: Exclusive: Chris Moore, running for the party in Greenvale, made derogatory social media comments between 2010 and 2012 Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast A One Nation candidate in Victoria has apologised for a series of offensive comments including repeated references to Australian-Indians as “curry munchers”, comparing a woman in burqa to a bag of rubbish, and sharing an image calling Julia Gillard a slut. The party’s candidate for Greenvale on Melbourne’s north-western fringe, Chris Moore, also made derogatory comments about lesbians and refugees and once posted that he “doesn’t like the way the new homo cleaner at work looks at me”. title: Bunny Shaw leads Manchester City to five‑star win as Chelsea draws with Everton
content:
On Women’s Football Weekly, Faye Carruthers hosts a podcast with Suzanne Wrack, Sophie Downey and Marva Kreel to discuss the weekend’s Women’s Super League action.  

The hosts highlight Manchester City’s five‑star performance, with Bunny Shaw shining again, while Chelsea suffered a frustrating afternoon, being held to a draw by Everton.  

Arsenal earned three points against Liverpool thanks to Alessia Russo’s two goals, while Beth England secured a late winner for Crystal Palace. Spurs and London City Lionesses also recorded victories.
summary: Bunny Shaw starred in Manchester City’s five‑star WSL win. Chelsea were held to a draw by Everton and Arsenal secured three points against Liverpool with two goals from Alessia Russo.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Premier League sees first 4-4 draw in August or September
content:
The Premier League has witnessed a rare 4-4 draw, a result that has occurred in only 19 of the 13,266 games played since the competition’s inception. This scoreline represents just 0.1% of all matches, contrasting sharply with the 1-0 result, which accounts for 17.6% of games. The article notes that this specific draw has never happened during August or September, months when teams are typically at peak fitness and motivation. Instead, 4-4 draws are more common in the second half of April, a period described as having an "on-the-beachness" where late-campaign football feels increasingly pointless as thoughts turn to the close season.

In a separate segment, the text highlights the pitch drop experiment at the University of Queensland, described as the world’s longest-running experiment. Initiated in 1930 to demonstrate how an apparent solid behaves like an extremely viscous liquid, the experiment involves pitch placed in a funnel at room temperature. The substance moves at a rate of approximately one atom per second, which is slower than continental drift. While nearly 100 years have passed since the experiment began, only nine drips have ever been recorded, and none have been witnessed directly.

The article concludes with a comparison between the two events, suggesting that the slow, uneventful nature of watching the pitch drop is similar to watching an Arsenal 1-0 victory. This analogy is attributed to John Holtom, who notes that without the need for intercontinental travel, readers can appreciate the tedium of such slow-moving events.
summary: Manchester United and Aston Villa produced a 4-4 draw, a scoreline that has never occurred in the Premier League during August or September. The article notes that 4-4 draws are rare, accounting for only 0.1% of the 13,266 games played since the league's inception.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick on the brink and Madrid on the charge under Mourinho
content: Football Weekly features Max Rushden joined by Nicky Bandini, Archie Rhind-Tutt, Philippe Auclair, and Sid Lowe. The episode discusses Michael Carrick’s impending departure from Manchester United and provides a summary of major football stories from across Europe.
summary: Max Rushden is joined by Nicky Bandini, Archie Rhind-Tutt, Philippe Auclair, and Sid Lowe for a wrap of big European stories. Michael Carrick looks set to leave Manchester United as Real Madrid is on the charge under Mourinho.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Noskova beats Gauff to reach WTA Finals semi-finals as Pegula stays alive
content:
Linda Noskova advanced to the WTA Finals semi-finals after defeating Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 on Tuesday. The Czech player, who previously defeated Marta Kostyuk in her opening match, has won both encounters without dropping a set, securing her place in the knockout stage. Meanwhile, Jessica Pegula eliminated Kostyuk with a straight-sets victory to remain in contention for the final berth.

Gauff and Pegula currently hold 1-1 records in the round-robin stage. The final matches scheduled for Thursday will determine which of the two players joins Noskova in the last four.
summary: Linda Noskova defeated Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 to secure her place in the WTA Finals semi-finals. Jessica Pegula advanced by defeating Marta Kostyuk in straight sets, leaving both players with 1-1 records ahead of the final round-robin matches.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cricket Australia's equivocation on ball tampering scandal prolongs controversy
content: The interminable sandpaper scandal will drag on to the next press conference, social media post or book, until it festers into something much bigger than it needs to be There are some stories that you look back on and wonder whether we lost our collective minds. In Australia, 2018 was not a good year for banking executives, for prime ministers, for oily lord mayors and for cardinals. But the greatest betrayal of trust apparently concerned our national cricket team. There was public bawling, righteous indignation, weasel words and sanctimonious pieties. Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull, flanked by a doleful Angus Taylor and a nodding firefighter, called it a “terrible disgrace”. “They now have to make sure this great national game, this great international game that is synonymous with fair play, is once again played by champions that everybody can look up to.” Turnbull was more of a sailing man anyway. His parliamentary tenure was the political equivalent of Graeme Hick’s cricket career. By the time he’d been punted from office four months later, the Australian cricket team was being reimagined. The Ethics Centre’s 116-page document used the “Everest Process” to ascertain Cricket Australia’s alignment with its ethical framework. There were lots of charts asking how well CA was adhering to this value or that. “Mostly not lived”, “sometimes lived” and “always lived” were some of the measures. One could have saved a lot of time, money and paper and simply concluded “don’t be a prick, don’t bark like a dog when an opponent is dismissed, and don’t shove sandpaper down your dacks”.
summary: Cricket Australia's equivocal response to the sandpaper scandal is prolonging the controversy and causing it to fester. The Ethics Centre's 116-page report assessed Cricket Australia's ethical alignment using the Everest Process.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Usman Khawaja adjusts book tour schedule amid ball-tampering claims
content:
Usman Khawaja’s promotional book tour has undergone schedule adjustments following his appearance on the ABC’s 7.30 Report. The former Australia Test batter was questioned regarding specific claims during the program, after which he withdrew from several radio and television engagements scheduled for Wednesday.

His publisher, Penguin, confirmed that the tour would not be cancelled entirely, though changes were made to his itinerary for the current week. Khawaja was described as evasive when responding to inquiries about the allegations raised during the broadcast.
summary: Usman Khawaja's promotional book tour has been adjusted after he was questioned on the ABC's 7.30 Report. His publisher Penguin confirmed that while the tour was not cancelled, he pulled out of some radio and television spots.
author: Guardian Sport

title: WSL Matchweek Nine: Shaw Hat-Trick and Lionesses Wonder Goal
content: Matchweek nine of the Women's Super League featured a first-half wonder goal by London City Lionesses and Khadija Shaw’s first hat-trick of the season. These highlights are part of a collection showcasing every goal from the recent round of matches.
summary: Khadija Shaw scored her first hat-trick of the Women's Super League season during matchweek nine. London City Lionesses also featured a first-half wonder goal in the matchweek's highlights.
author: BBC Sport

title: Plymouth Parkway beat Berkhamsted 2-1 in extra time to reach FA Cup second round
content: Plymouth Parkway advanced to the FA Cup second round for the first time in club history after defeating Berkhamsted 2-1 in extra time. The match featured two penalties scored by Andrew Neal, which allowed Plymouth Parkway to overcome an initial goal deficit and secure their victory.
summary: Plymouth Parkway defeated Berkhamsted 2-1 in extra time to secure a spot in the FA Cup second round. Two penalties from Andrew Neal helped Plymouth Parkway come from a goal down to earn the victory.
author: BBC Sport

title: BBC Sport visits Shea and Pierce Charles at their London home
content: BBC Sport visited Shea and Pierce Charles at their London home ahead of Northern Ireland's Nations League matches. The brothers discussed topics including birthdays, steak sandwiches, and their roles in Michael O'Neill's young team.
summary: BBC Sport joins Shea and Pierce Charles at their London home before Northern Ireland's Nations League matches. The brothers discuss birthdays, steak sandwiches, and their roles in Michael O'Neill's young team.
author: BBC Sport

title: Best FA Cup first round goals: Seung-woo Yang and Charlie McNeill
content: The article highlights the most memorable goals from the FA Cup first round. It features Seung‑woo Yang’s strike for Wimborne Town and a remarkable halfway‑line effort by Crewe’s Charlie McNeill.
summary: The article highlights the best goals from the first round of the FA Cup, featuring Seung-woo Yang's goal for Wimborne Town. It also mentions an effort from the halfway line by Crewe's Charlie McNeill.
