title: Ultrarunner Stephanie Case Becomes First Woman to Run 100 Miles in Antarctica
content:
Ultrarunner Stephanie Case became the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica, a milestone she discussed with BBC Sport.

She said she wanted to prove to every mother that motherhood is not the finish line and that they can go out and do big adventures and dream big.
summary: Stephanie Case became the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica. She told BBC Sport that she wanted to prove to every mother in the world that motherhood is not the finish line and that they can go out and do big adventures and dream big.
author: BBC Sport

title: Chelsea Hold Hacken to Goalless Draw, Keep Unbeaten in Women's Champions League
content: Chelsea secured a goalless draw against Hacken, keeping their unbeaten run in the Women’s Champions League intact. The match saw Hacken earn their second point of the season, while Chelsea remained frustrated by the stalemate.
summary: Chelsea held Hacken to a goalless draw in the Women's Champions League. The match gave Hacken their second point of the season while Chelsea kept their unbeaten start.
author: BBC Sport

title: Cruz warns Hegseth will resign, be fired or face impeachment
content: The Hill’s Defense & National Security newsletter reports that Sen. Ted Cruz (R‑Texas) said on his podcast earlier this week that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will either resign, be fired or be impeached.
summary: Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) predicted on his podcast earlier this week that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will either resign, be fired or be impeached. The prediction was made during a podcast discussion.
author: The Hill

title: Nixon Calls Florida Senate Race a Missed Opportunity for Democrats
content: Florida Senate candidate Angie Nixon (D), who lost to GOP incumbent Sen. Ashley Moody in last week’s midterm elections, called the race a “missed opportunity” for Sunshine State Democrats. In an interview posted Tuesday, Nixon stated that if Democrats want to profess caring about Black people and Hispanic communities, they need to take specific actions.
summary: Florida Senate candidate Angie Nixon (D) lost to GOP incumbent Sen. Ashley Moody in last week's midterm elections. In an interview posted Tuesday, Nixon called the contest a "missed opportunity" for Sunshine State Democrats.
author: The Hill

title: Ken Calvert projected to win California’s merged 40th District race
content: Republican Rep. Ken Calvert is projected to defeat fellow California Republican Rep. Young Kim in the race for the state’s 40th Congressional District. According to preliminary results from Decision Desk HQ, Calvert leads by about 69 percent reporting. The contest was determined by the passage of Proposition 50 in California last year.
summary: Rep. Ken Calvert (R-Calif.) is projected to win the race for California’s 40th Congressional District against fellow California Republican Rep.
author: The Hill

title: Kennedy family joins legal fight over Trump’s proposed arch
content: Kennedy family members have entered a legal dispute over President Trump’s proposed arch. In a Monday court filing in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia, the family asked the court to bar the Trump administration from taking any steps to approve, authorize, or construct the arch.
summary: The Kennedy family has joined a legal battle against President Trump’s proposed arch. In a court filing on Monday in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia, they requested that the court bar the Trump administration from taking any steps to approve, authorize, or construct the arch.
author: The Hill

title: Senate Advances Permitting Reform Bill One Step Closer to Finish
content: The Senate advanced a major infrastructure and energy bill Tuesday night via a 62-21 procedural vote. The legislation aims to accelerate the construction of energy and other projects while limiting environmental challenges, moving the bill one step closer to completion in the upper chamber.
summary: The Senate advanced a major infrastructure and energy bill in a procedural vote of 62-21. The bill aims to speed up the buildout of energy and other projects while curtailing environmental challenges.
author: The Hill

title: Reporters Without Borders urges impeachment of FCC Chair Brendan Carr
content: Reporters Without Borders is urging the incoming Congress to impeach Federal Communications Commission Chair Brendan Carr, alleging that he has undermined press freedom by punishing news outlets critical of President Trump and his administration. The organization says Carr has repeatedly used the FCC’s regulatory authority to pursue politically motivated actions.
summary: Reporters Without Borders is urging the incoming Congress to impeach FCC Chair Brendan Carr. The group says Carr has undermined press freedom by using the FCC to punish news outlets critical of President Trump and his administration.
author: The Hill

title: House Democrat Stansbury Misses Vote on Hegseth Impeachment Block Due to Traffic Incident
content: Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N. M.) stated on Tuesday that a traffic incident and police escort prevented her and other lawmakers from reaching the Capitol in time to vote. She said these delays stopped them from voting against a Republican effort to block the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
summary: House Democrat Stansbury Misses Vote on Hegseth Impeachment Block Due to Traffic Incident.
author: The Hill

title: Dean Says She’s Considering Challenging Fetterman in 2028
content: Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) stated on Tuesday that she is “considering” challenging Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) in the 2028 election. In an interview with Politico, Dean noted her concerns regarding Fetterman’s family and health as motivations for potentially entering the race. Her comments come as other Democrats weigh bids to unseat the incumbent.
summary: Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) said Tuesday she is “considering” challenging Sen.
author: The Hill

title: House Oversight Committee Faults Federal Government Over Epstein Accountability
content: The House Oversight Committee released a report detailing its investigation into sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The committee faulted the federal government for failing to hold the financier accountable.
summary: The House Oversight Committee released a report into its investigation into sex‑offender Jeffrey Epstein. The committee faulted the federal government for not holding the financier accountable.
author: NPR Politics

title: Supreme Court hears arguments on temporary worker visa enforcement case
content: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case concerning temporary worker visas, with the justices appearing divided over federal agencies’ authority to impose fines for law violations. The company involved argued that enforcement issues should be addressed through the courts rather than by the federal agency alone.
summary: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.
author: NPR Politics

title: House votes to end impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
content: House Republicans short-circuited a floor vote on the impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The initiative had been brought by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie, but the party managed to effectively end the proceeding.
summary: House Republicans short-circuited a floor vote on the impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The impeachment effort was brought against Hegseth by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.
author: NPR Politics

title: Hegseth remains defiant as Congress deliberates impeachment articles
content: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth held his first press conference in months as members of Congress began deliberating on articles of impeachment against him. During the event, Hegseth fought back, maintaining a defiant stance amid the ongoing legislative proceedings.
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is fighting back as Congress begins deliberating on impeachment articles against him. He gave his first press conference in months.
author: NPR Politics

title: Thousands of one-flowered wintergreens rescued from eroding Scottish coast
content:
Conservationists have relocated 3,400 one-flowered wintergreen plants from the eroding shoreline of Culbin Forest in Moray, Scotland. The intervention was undertaken to protect the wildflowers from falling into the sea due to coastal erosion.

The one-flowered wintergreen is considered one of Britain’s rarest wildflowers. The species is estimated to have lost more than half of its UK population over the past 50 years, prompting efforts to rescue the plants at risk on the Scottish coast.
summary: Conservationists moved 3,400 one-flowered wintergreen plants to safety at Culbin Forest in Moray after erosion threatened them. The species has lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years.
author: Guardian Environment

title: University of Zurich finds biomarker extends GHB detection window
content:
Researchers at the University of Zurich are testing a new biomarker that could extend the detection window for the date‑rape drug GHB. The drug is often used to render victims unconscious, but it is excreted quickly from blood and urine, making timely detection difficult.

The team has been evaluating the biomarker with urine samples taken from real forensic cases. Their preliminary findings suggest that the marker can signal earlier GHB intake even when conventional analyses no longer detect the drug.
summary: Researchers at the University of Zurich evaluated a new biomarker using urine samples from real forensic cases. The biomarker can indicate earlier GHB intake even when the drug is no longer detectable with conventional analysis.
author: Medical Xpress

title: BGU Study Links Metabolic Memory to Weight Gain Post Sleep Apnea Treatment
content:
A recent study by Ben‑Gurion University of the Negev and Soroka University Medical Center has explored why many adults and children gain weight after successful treatment for obstructive sleep apnea. The research, carried out on mice, was published in Scientific Reports and investigates the biological mechanisms that may underlie this phenomenon.

The authors found that the body retains a persistent “metabolic memory” after normal breathing is restored. This memory appears to continue driving increased appetite, potentially leading to weight gain even after sleep apnea has been effectively treated.
summary: A study by Ben‑Gurion University of the Negev and Soroka University Medical Center found that mice retained a persistent metabolic memory that drives increased appetite after successful treatment of obstructive sleep apnea. The research, published in Scientific Reports, suggests this mechanism may explain why adults and children gain weight following treatment.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Finds Weekly Park Visits May Boost Children's Mental Health
content:
A new University of Exeter study suggests that children who visit parks and playgrounds at least once a week may experience improved mental health and social development as they grow up. The research, which examines long‑term outcomes, indicates a positive link between regular park visits and children’s well‑being.

The findings were published in the journal Epidemiology and Community Health in a paper titled “Park Visits and Social‑Emotional Development throughout Childhood: A Longitudinal Analysis of ALSPAC.”
summary: Children who visit parks and playgrounds at least once a week may have better mental health and social development as they grow up. That's according to a new study by the University of Exeter, published in Epidemiology and Community Health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Pregnant Women with Cannabis Use Disorder More Likely to Seek Postpartum Psychiatric ER Care
content: A study of more than 2 million California deliveries found that women diagnosed with cannabis use disorder during pregnancy were more likely to visit an emergency room for a psychiatric problem within the year after giving birth. The research links cannabis addiction in pregnancy to an increased risk of postpartum psychiatric crises.
summary: Women diagnosed with cannabis use disorder during pregnancy were more likely to visit an emergency room for a psychiatric problem within the year after giving birth. The finding comes from a study of more than 2 million California deliveries.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Family and Friends Shape Dementia Care Decisions
content: Decisions about dementia care can significantly affect a person’s health and quality of life. The article explores how these choices are made, focusing on the role of family members and friends in the decision‑making process.
summary: Decisions about dementia care affect a person's health and quality of life. The article explores how these decisions are made when family members or friends are involved.
author: Medical Xpress

title: School bullying linked to PTSD symptoms and diagnosis
content:
School bullying has been linked to lower academic achievement and increased mental health problems, underscoring its importance as a concern for educational psychology.  

Understanding the psychological consequences of bullying is essential for educators, school psychologists, and policymakers, who must develop effective interventions that support students’ well‑being and learning outcomes.  

An ongoing debate centers on whether bullying qualifies as a traumatic event that can lead to posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: School bullying has been linked to lower academic achievement and increased mental health problems, raising concerns in educational psychology. The debate continues over whether bullying qualifies as a traumatic event that could lead to posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms and diagnosis.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Zealand Study Finds Major Gaps in Women’s Heart Health Care
content:
A systematic review covering 25 years of New Zealand research has highlighted significant gaps in women’s heart‑health care. Published in the New Zealand Medical Journal, the study points to opportunities to improve diagnosis, treatment and outcomes for women with cardiovascular disease.  

Co‑led by Dr Kylie Short of Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury, the review identified a pronounced gender data gap: only 26 % of the studies examined differences between women and men.
summary: A systematic review of 25 years of New Zealand research, published in the New Zealand Medical Journal, found significant gaps in women’s heart health care. The review, co-led by Dr. Kylie Short of Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury, noted that only 26% of studies focused on gender differences.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New organic iron-sulfur framework boosts photosynthesis and carbon fixation
content: A new organic iron‑sulfur framework has been developed that enhances photosynthesis and carbon fixation. Iron‑sulfur clusters are ancient protein cofactors essential for electron transport, enzyme catalysis and photosynthesis. Their sensitivity to oxygen and inherent instability, however, have long limited their practical application.
summary: Iron-sulfur clusters are ancient protein cofactors essential for electron transport, enzyme catalysis, and photosynthesis. Their sensitivity to oxygen and inherent instability have long hindered practical applications.
author: Phys.org

title: Earliest known compact quasar pair found 900 million years after Big Bang
content:
Astronomers have identified the oldest pair of compact quasars ever observed, located only 900 million years after the Big Bang.  

Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the pair of actively feeding black holes grew so massive at such an early time in the history of the universe. The quasars have been given the Hawaiian nickname Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
summary: Astronomers have identified the oldest known pair of compact quasars, observed just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the actively feeding black holes grew so massive, and the pair has been nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
author: Phys.org

title: Genetic Ancestry Drives Cory's Shearwater Migration More Than Social Environment
content:
A new study published in the journal Molecular Ecology examines the drivers of long‑distance migration in seabirds. The research focuses on Cory's shearwater, a species whose migratory routes remain poorly understood.  

The authors report that an individual’s genetic ancestry has a stronger influence on its migratory decisions than the social environment within its breeding colony. This finding suggests that inherited genetic factors play a key role in shaping the migratory behaviour of Cory's shearwaters.
summary: A study published in the journal Molecular Ecology shows that for Cory's shearwater, genetic ancestry is a more significant factor in migratory decisions than the social environment of the breeding colony. The findings indicate that genes play a key role in the migration of this seabird species.
author: Phys.org

title: ZonationR streamlines biodiversity conservation planning with automated workflow
content: ZonationR is a new tool that simplifies the use of Zonation to identify priority areas for biodiversity conservation. It consolidates all stages of the conservation planning analysis into a single automated, reproducible workflow, enabling users to systematically explore and compare alternative conservation scenarios.
summary: ZonationR is a new tool that simplifies the use of Zonation to identify priority areas for biodiversity conservation. It brings all stages of the conservation planning analysis together in one automated and reproducible workflow and helps users systematically explore and compare alternative conservation scenarios.
author: Phys.org

title: Mental Health App DRIVEN Shows Promise in Helping Unemployed Find Jobs, Six-Week Trial
content: A six‑week clinical trial led by Northwestern University tested a phone app called DRIVEN. The app delivers weekly self‑guided mental‑health exercises aimed at reducing stress and boosting motivation, and pairs these with job‑seeking strategies. Early results suggest the intervention may help unemployed individuals secure employment.
summary: A Northwestern University–led clinical trial found that the phone app DRIVEN, which offers weekly self-guided mental health exercises and job‑seeking strategies, may help break the cycle of depression and unemployment. The six‑week trial indicates the app could help unemployed people find jobs.
author: Phys.org

title: PSI study reduces four hybrid LCA methods to two, easing product impact assessment
content:
Life cycle assessment (LCA) is a key tool for measuring the environmental impact of products and services and is often used as a basis for policy decisions. Yet collecting the necessary data for a full LCA is notoriously difficult.  

A recent study from the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) demonstrates that four established hybrid LCA methods can be consolidated into just two. The researchers describe this simplification as a first step toward open‑source software that would allow such analyses to be performed even by users lacking advanced mathematical expertise.
summary: Life cycle assessment quantifies environmental impacts of products and services and informs political decisions, but data capture is difficult. A study by the Paul Scherrer Institute PSI shows that four established hybrid methods can be reduced to two, a first step toward open‑source software that could enable analyses without in‑depth mathematical knowledge.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds coyotes persist on Outer Banks despite removal efforts
content: A new study shows that coyote populations on North Carolina’s Outer Banks continue to thrive despite ongoing removal efforts, posing a persistent threat to shore‑nesting birds and protected sea turtles. The research is the first in‑depth assessment of coyote numbers on barrier islands and highlights broader ecological implications.
summary: A new study shows coyote populations on the Outer Banks of North Carolina continue despite ongoing removal programs. Researchers note the coyotes pose a continued threat to shore‑nesting birds and protected sea turtles, and the study is the first in‑depth assessment of coyotes on barrier islands.
author: Phys.org

title: German VAT cut in 2020 significantly boosted private consumption, study finds
content:
A study published in the Review of Economic Studies examines the impact of Germany’s summer‑2020 value‑added tax reduction, which lowered the rate from 19 % to 16 % for six months as part of the country’s COVID‑19 economic stimulus package. Using survey data, retail‑purchase records and an economic model, the researchers assess how the temporary cut affected private consumption.

The analysis shows that the tax cut most strongly boosted spending among lower‑wealth households and among younger and middle‑aged families, with the effect appearing independent of respondents’ financial‑literacy levels.
summary: The German federal government lowered the value-added tax from 19% to 16% for half a year in summer 2020 as part of its COVID economic stimulus package. A study published in Review of Economic Studies found the cut markedly increased private consumption, with lower‑wealth, younger and middle‑aged households benefiting regardless of financial literacy.
author: Phys.org

title: Review of 350 studies links lower protein intake to slower aging
content: A major review of more than 350 studies finds that eating less protein could slow aging, improve metabolic health and potentially extend lifespan, challenging the belief that higher protein intake is always beneficial. Researchers caution that many sedentary adults may be consuming excess protein, and note that protein needs vary with age and physical activity.
summary: A review of over 350 studies suggests that eating less protein could slow aging, improve metabolic health, and potentially extend lifespan. Researchers caution that many sedentary adults may consume too much protein and note that protein needs vary by age and activity level.
author: Science Daily

title: Astronomers detect hidden exoplanet using James Webb digital twin technique
content: Astronomers have identified a previously hidden exoplanet in images from the James Webb Space Telescope. The discovery resulted from a new imaging technique that employs a digital twin of the telescope to subtract the intense glare of host stars, a process that makes faint planets two to fifteen times easier to detect than with standard methods. Researchers say the approach has already revealed the concealed planet in existing data and holds promise for uncovering many additional worlds.
summary: Scientists developed a technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove star glare, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than conventional methods. The method has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data.
author: Science Daily

title: Global fossil fuel emissions projected to fall in 2026 while total CO2 rises
content:
Global fossil‑fuel emissions are projected to decline in 2026, driven by growth in renewable energy and electric vehicles, according to the latest forecasts.  At the same time, emissions from deforestation are rising, creating the risk that total CO₂ output could reach a new record despite the drop in fossil‑fuel use.

Scientists caution that the remaining carbon budget needed to limit warming to 1.5 °C could be exhausted in less than four years, even as a sustained decline in overall emissions appears increasingly possible.
summary: Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall in 2026 as renewable energy and electric vehicles gain ground. However, rising emissions from deforestation could push total CO2 emissions to a new record, and scientists say the remaining carbon budget for limiting warming to 1.5°C could be exhausted in less than four years.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA launches $500,000 AMPERE Challenge for electric rocket engine development
content: NASA has launched the AMPERE Challenge, a competition that puts $500,000 at stake to speed development of advanced electric rocket engines for satellites and future space exploration. The program will award cash prizes and NASA testing‑facility access to up to two U.S. companies, aiming to move promising propulsion technologies toward real‑world missions.
summary: NASA is putting $500,000 on the line in a new competition to accelerate the development of advanced electric rocket engines for satellites and future space exploration. The AMPERE Challenge will reward up to two U.
author: Science Daily

title: Four NASA volunteers end CHAPEA Mars simulation after more than a year
content: Four NASA volunteers who spent more than a year in a simulated Mars habitat have emerged from isolation, concluding the CHAPEA experiment. During the mission they grew food, conserved resources and tackled challenges designed to mimic conditions on Mars, providing data that NASA says may aid preparation for future human activities on the Moon and Mars.
summary: Four NASA volunteers emerged from isolation after more than a year of simulated life on Mars, ending the CHAPEA experiment. Their experiences growing food, conserving resources and overcoming Mars‑like challenges could help NASA prepare for humanity’s future on the Moon and Mars.
author: Science Daily

title: 237‑million‑year‑old armored sea amphibian fossils found in China
content: Fossils dating to 237 million years ago show a heavily armored amphibian that lived in the oceans. The creature, comparable in size to a giant salamander, was discovered in China and may represent the first known amphibian to have fully adapted to a marine environment, a capability absent in modern amphibians.
summary: Fossils of a heavily armored amphibian that lived in the oceans 237 million years ago have been discovered in China. The giant salamander‑sized creature may represent the first known amphibian to have fully adapted to a marine environment.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists identify fat particles that cause heart attacks despite low bad cholesterol
content: Scientists have found that heart attacks can occur even when “bad” cholesterol is reduced to healthy levels. Their research identified two kinds of fat‑carrying particles that seem to trigger inflammation and damage blood vessels by mechanisms that operate independently of cholesterol accumulation.
summary: Even when bad cholesterol is reduced to healthy levels, some individuals still face risk of heart attacks. Researchers found two types of fat‑carrying particles that may promote inflammation and damage blood vessels through mechanisms beyond cholesterol buildup.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists uncover 66‑pound giant rodent Yakamys sirindhornae from Thailand
content: Scientists have uncovered fossils of a giant rodent in Thailand that lived 34 million years ago. The species, named Yakamys sirindhornae, is estimated to have weighed about 66 pounds—roughly twice the size of other known rodents of its time—showing that enormous rodents evolved much earlier than previously thought.
summary: Scientists uncovered fossils of a giant rodent that lived in Thailand 34 million years ago. The species, named Yakamys sirindhornae, may have weighed about 66 pounds, roughly twice the weight of other known rodents of its time.
author: Science Daily

title: Bambu Lab P2S Combo 3D printer discounted $100, now $649 at Best Buy
content:
The Bambu Lab P2S Combo is being offered at a reduced price through December 1. The bundle, which pairs the Bambu P2S printer with the AMS 2 Pro multi‑filament handler, is listed for $649 at both Best Buy and directly from Bambu Lab, representing a $100 discount off the standard bundle price.

The P2S printer supports multi‑color printing and includes an automatic material‑drying system intended to improve print quality. Its hardware features a 5‑inch touchscreen, a built‑in camera for remote monitoring, and AI‑powered tools that can detect printing problems. Additional conveniences include automatic bed leveling with a warning for a missing plate, a live camera feed for timelapse sharing, and a suite of sensors designed to keep prints running smoothly.

The AMS 2 Pro filament handler provides a fully enclosed environment that protects filament from moisture and reduces nozzle or tube clogs. It is priced at $229 during the promotion, down from its usual $299, and the P2S printer can accommodate up to four such units simultaneously, allowing weeks‑long intervals between filament changes.

Separately, the P2S printer alone is normally $549 and is also listed at $100 off during the same period. A colleague, Sean Hollister, noted the printer’s consistency and hands‑off operation.
summary: The Bambu P2S Combo. | Image: Bambu If you’re tired of filament jams and clogged nozzles, perhaps it’s time for a new 3D printer.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft launches Auto SR upscaling for Xbox Ally X, now works handheld
content:
Microsoft announced that its Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR) technology, positioned as an upscaling rival to Nvidia’s DLSS, is now available for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and certain Windows Copilot Plus PCs. The rollout includes new features for the system, extending the functionality that was previously limited to docked use.

During testing in April, Auto SR could be used on the Xbox Ally X only while the device was docked. The full release now enables the feature to operate while the console is in handheld mode and running on battery power, and it also supports games rendered at 1080p resolution. Microsoft cautioned that using Auto SR in handheld mode at 1080p may affect performance.
summary: The Xbox Ally X. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge Microsoft is now rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), an upscaling technology that competes with Nvidia's DLSS, for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs, the company announced today.
author: The Verge

title: Apple M6 entry‑level 14‑inch MacBook Pro reviewed as good but lacking new features
content:
A review of Apple’s entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro notes that the device occupies an uncomfortable position between the MacBook Air and higher-end models. The review highlights that this year’s model features the Apple M6 chip, which is described as great, and may offer fringe benefits unavailable in top-tier configurations. However, the laptop retains the same MacBook Pro design Apple has used since 2021, lacking newer features such as a touchscreen, OLED panel, Dynamic Island, weight reduction, or a glowing Apple logo.

The review contrasts this with previous entry-level models, such as the 13-inch M1 and M2 MacBook Pros, which retained older 2016-era designs, including the Touch Bar. It observes that Apple frequently reserves its most updated designs and screen technologies for more expensive high-end models, while lesser versions stick with older designs or other compromises. The M6 chip is noted to potentially lack Pro, Max, or Ultra configurations, distinguishing it from the top-tier MacBook Pros.
summary: Apple M6 entry‑level 14‑inch MacBook Pro reviewed as good but lacking new features.
author: Ars Technica

title: US Republicans Block Impeachment Effort Against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth Over Iran War
content: US Defence chief Hegseth defended operations he led in Yemen, Iran and against alleged drug smugglers, stating, "I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow," while portraying the impeachment effort as an attack on US troops.
summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth defended operations he led in Yemen, Iran, and against alleged drug smugglers, saying he stands behind them and would repeat them. He portrayed the impeachment effort as an attack on US troops.
author: Euronews

title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran ops unnecessary, urges broader Russia‑Ukraine talks
content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a press conference on Tuesday as the G7 meets in Paris. He said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because economic restrictions were working so effectively.

Rubio also hailed US‑mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi as “very productive” and said the discussions should be expanded to include Europeans at the table.
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio talked to the press Tuesday as the G7 meets in Paris. He said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because economic restrictions were working so effectively.
author: France 24

title: France summons Iran's ambassador over hacked supermarket refrigerators
content: France, acting on U.S. intelligence, summoned Iran’s ambassador after a hack last month caused hundreds of supermarket refrigerators to overheat, with fifteen units catching fire. The incident highlights growing cyber‑attack concerns in Europe, as authorities link the sabotage to Tehran amid Iran’s efforts to end its international isolation.
summary: France, reportedly acting on US intelligence, summoned Tehran’s ambassador over a hacking incident. The hack caused hundreds of supermarket refrigerators to overheat last month, with 15 catching fire.
author: France 24

title: US Army senior member arrested in Britain on suspicion of aiding Russian intelligence
content: UK police arrested a senior member of the US Army on Tuesday on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence. The 41‑year‑old was detained near Gloucester, west England, and remains in custody. The arrest is not related to other counter‑terror investigations.
summary: UK police arrested a senior member of the US Army on Tuesday on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence. The 41-year-old was detained near Gloucester in west England and remains in custody, and the arrest is not related to other counter-terror investigations.
author: France 24

title: Sophos expert warns French supermarket refrigeration cyberattack caused food loss
content:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Rafe Pilling, Director of Threat Intelligence in the Sophos Counter Threat Unit (CTU), to discuss how a minor cyber intrusion can disrupt food supplies, expose industrial infrastructure weaknesses, and serve geopolitical aims. Pilling highlighted recent attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems in France as a clear example of digital vulnerabilities turning into real‑world economic disruption.

According to Pilling, an adversary needs only a small amount of effort to create a large impact. In the French case, the attacks destroyed food, left shelves empty, and caused refrigeration units in stores to fail. The incident shows how modest technical interventions can produce disproportionate economic and operational consequences.

Pilling’s remarks underscore the asymmetry at the core of contemporary cyber conflict: small, targeted actions can generate significant disruption, illustrating the broader threat that cyberattacks pose to society and infrastructure.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Rafe Pilling, Director of Threat Intelligence in the Sophos Counter Threat Unit (CTU). Pilling said cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems in France can, with modest effort, destroy food and create empty shelves, illustrating asymmetric cyberwarfare.
author: France 24

title: Haiti PM praises Bukele after Salvadoran troops destroy gang leader's home
content:
Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils‑Aime praised Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele on Tuesday after Salvadoran troops destroyed a suspected gang leader’s home.  

Bukele’s deployment of more than 2,000 soldiers, prompted by the disappearance of four Salvadoran troops, has raised concerns over rules of engagement and coordination with a UN‑backed force fighting Haiti’s gangs.
summary: Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime praised Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele after Salvadoran troops destroyed a suspected gang leader’s home. Bukele’s deployment of more than 2,000 soldiers following four Salvadoran troops’ disappearance has raised concerns over rules of engagement and coordination with a UN‑backed force combating Haiti’s gangs.
author: France 24

title: Migrant boat capsizes off Senegal's northwest coast, 39 dead
content:
A migrant boat capsized off Senegal’s northwest coast, killing at least 39 people. The incident is reported as one of the country’s deadliest migration tragedies in recent years.

The report notes that the story will explore why so many continue to risk their lives, featuring a guest interview with Aissata Kane of the International Organization for Migration.  

The article also references other unrelated events, including a deadly attack in western Ethiopia that left 65 people dead, violence near the Sudanese border, and recent taekwondo results at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.
summary: At least 39 people died after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal's northwest coast. It is described as one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years.
author: France 24

title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah faces prison in retrial over licence and false news charges
content: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, head of independent outlet Mada Masr, is scheduled for a criminal court retrial on Wednesday on charges of operating without a licence and publishing false news. The United Nations criticised Egypt’s “widening assaults on press freedom” on Tuesday. Attalah previously received a one‑year prison sentence in absentia in 2024, and the trial has sparked international outcry.
summary: Lina Attalah, head of the independent news outlet Mada Masr, is facing a criminal court retrial on Wednesday on charges of operating without a licence and publishing false news. The United Nations criticised Egypt’s widening assaults on press freedom, and Attalah had previously received a one‑year prison sentence in absentia in 2024.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine and Russia hold second day of US‑mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
content: Ukraine and Russia are holding the second day of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. On the first day, Washington urged a “new” security framework, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was “happy” with the mediators’ changed approach. The negotiations are scheduled to continue on Wednesday.
summary: Washington called for a new security framework on the first day of US‑led talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was happy with the changes in approach by US mediators and negotiations will continue Wednesday.
author: France 24

title: Thousands in Gaza lack shelter as 150,000 tents await Israeli approval
content:
Charities warn that more than 940,000 displaced Palestinians are living in flood‑prone areas without adequate protection, raising health concerns. Tens of thousands remain in water‑logged and damaged tents after heavy rains and wind battered the Gaza Strip over the weekend, and at least four children and one woman have been killed.

Aid agencies say 150,000 new shelters are positioned outside Gaza but await Israeli approval before they can be brought in. Meanwhile, thousands are without shelter as sanitation infrastructure has been destroyed, leaving sewage to flow into the remaining tents.
summary: Charities say over 940,000 displaced Palestinians are in flood‑prone areas with water‑logged, damaged tents after weekend storms in Gaza. 150,000 new tents are held outside Gaza for Israeli approval while thousands remain without shelter and sanitation, and at least four Palestinian children and a woman have been killed.
author: Guardian World

title: Judge lets Donald Trump's $10 bn defamation suit against BBC move forward
content: Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. The president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit stems from the BBC’s splicing together of disparate comments he made before the 6 January US Capitol insurrection, as rendered in a Panorama documentary called Trump: A Second Chance. “Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the Court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” the Trump-appointed Florida district court judge wrote. “It would be difficult for the Court to accept a different framing without completely negating the significance and fragility of political elections.”
summary: Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denied the BBC's motion to dismiss, allowing Donald Trump's $10 bn defamation lawsuit to proceed. The suit claims the BBC's Panorama documentary "Trump: A Second Chance" spliced together comments he made before the Jan. 6 Capitol insurrection, causing reputational harm.
author: Guardian World

title: Foo Fighters pause Sydney show to honor Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell
content:
Foo Fighters paused their Sydney concert on Tuesday night to honor Todd Russell, a survivor of the Beaconsfield mine collapse who died this week at age 54 from illness. Frontman Dave Grohl addressed the crowd, describing Russell as a “big” hero of his, and delivered a lengthy on‑stage tribute that broke up an otherwise raucous show.

The band, touring Australia for the 16th time in their 32‑year history, incorporated the solemn moment into the performance after the announcement of Russell’s death.
summary: Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl gave a lengthy on‑stage tribute to Todd Russell, a Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor, after news of Russell’s death at age 54 was announced. The tribute took place during the band’s Sydney concert, part of their Australian tour.
author: Guardian World

title: Mick Gatto gave gold bracelet to CFMEU official after site assault, royal commission hears
content:
Former Construction, Forestry, Maritime, and Energy Union (CFMEU) official Paul Tzimas testified before Victoria’s royal commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure projects. Tzimas said he sustained a fractured ankle when he and a colleague were seriously assaulted at a construction site; the colleague suffered major injuries and severe post‑traumatic stress disorder.

Tzimas added that underworld figure Mick Gatto attended a meeting convened after the attack and later offered him a gold bracelet. He is the first CFMEU‑linked witness to appear before the inquiry.
summary: Former CFMEU official Paul Tzimas told the royal commission he suffered a fractured ankle and a colleague sustained major injuries and severe PTSD after a construction site assault. He said underworld figure Mick Gatto attended a meeting after the assault and later offered him a gold bracelet.
author: Guardian World

title: Labor rejects antisemitism envoy's call to replace ABC and SBS ombudsmen
content:
The Albanese government has decided not to replace the ABC and SBS ombudsmen with an external oversight body, despite a suggestion from the antisemitism envoy. The decision follows an updated list of priorities released last month.

Jillian Segal, in the updated report released a fortnight ago, proposed transferring powers to an external independent ombudsman to monitor ABC and SBS coverage of the war in Gaza and to ensure publicly funded broadcasters are held accountable to their stated standards of accuracy and impartiality. Government sources note that a media regulator already exists.
summary: The Albanese government said it will not scrap the ABC and SBS ombudsmen as suggested by antisemitism envoy Jillian Segal. Segal’s updated report proposed an external independent ombudsman to monitor the broadcasters’ Gaza war coverage and enforce standards of accuracy and impartiality.
author: Guardian World

title: David Jones to close half of its stores, prompting mass job losses
content: Australia’s oldest department store collapsed into voluntary administration last week after years of steep losses Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast David Jones is set to shutter half of its department store network, triggering mass job losses under a sweeping restructure, the appointed receivers said on Wednesday. David Jones employs more than 6,000 staff across 38 stores.
summary: Australia’s oldest department store entered voluntary administration last week after years of steep losses. Receivers said David Jones will shutter half of its 38 stores, affecting more than 6,000 employees.
author: Guardian World

title: Youpla Group directors banned, fined $90,000 after funeral fund collapse
content:
Three directors of the collapsed funeral fund that marketed insurance to Aboriginal families have been penalised by a federal court. The court ordered a combined fine of $90,000 and disqualified the directors from managing any corporation for a period ranging from five to ten years.  

On Wednesday, Justice Geoffrey Kennett directed former Youpla Group director Jonathan Law—previously the director of the Aboriginal Community Benefit Fund (ACBF)—to pay the Commonwealth $50,000 and barred him from corporate management for six years. The ruling was based on breaches of duty to the fund’s clients.
summary: Three directors of the collapsed Youpla Group funeral fund were ordered to pay a combined $90,000 and were disqualified from managing corporations for at least five years. Federal Court Justice Geoffrey Kennett specifically ordered former director Jonathan Law to pay $50,000 and be barred from managing corporations for six years.
author: Guardian World

title: Ukraine captures first Indonesian POW amid rise in Russian recruitment
content:
Ukraine’s state‑run “I Want to Live” project says Ukrainian forces have captured the first Indonesian prisoner of war. The 49‑year‑old man, a native of Java, was taken to the Zaporizhzhia region to participate in a Russian assault. After his unit was hit by a drone attack, he reached Ukrainian‑held territory and was subsequently taken into custody.

Ukraine adds the capture comes as it reports a surge in Russian recruitment of citizens from Indonesia.
summary: Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, a 49-year-old man from Java. He had been taken to the Zaporizhzhia region for a Russian assault, reached Ukrainian-held territory after his group was hit by a drone attack, and was then captured.
author: Guardian World

title: US DOJ says three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks, including RAF Fairford incident
content: The U.S. Department of Justice says three Iran‑backed suspects plotted a series of attacks, one of which was a major incident near RAF Fairford, the United Kingdom airbase used by U.S. armed forces. The department identified the men as part of a string of plots targeting the site.
summary: The US Department of Justice says three Iran‑backed men were involved in a string of plots. One of the plots was a major incident near the UK airbase used by US armed forces.

title: Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo reveal why they joined Andy Weir's sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' (interview)
content: In any respectable audiobook project, finding the names of Andy Weir ("The Martian," "Project Hail Mary") and Benjamin Percy ("The Ninth Metal," "Wolverine") attached would elicit intense fan interest, but add the superstar vocal talents of Anthony Mackie ("Avengers: Infinity War," "Avengers: Doomsday"), Ariana DeBose ("West Side Story"), and John Leguizamo ("Ice Age"), and it catapults this sonic odyssey into the stratosphere. Such is the case with " Exoplanet," Audible Original’s new 7-episode science fiction audio drama executive produced by Weir and penned by Percy. Its planet-hopping space disaster narrative sees the crew of the starship Wild Blue Yonder hit a quantum anomaly, forcing their ship to crash-land onto a deadly exoplanet. All is not as it seems, though, as each crew member arrives in a different era on the same world. We hooked up with Mackie, DeBose, and Lequizamo to learn more about this renaissance of audio dramas and what attracted them to board Weir's sci-fi thriller. One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone. A sci-fi thriller executive produced by Andy Weir (#1 bestselling author of Project Hail Mary, The Martian ), with an all-star cast led by Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose and John Leguizamo. Exoplanet is free for Audible members, but also available for purchase separately. View Deal Mackie voices Chief Engineer Jeff Shaw. His attraction to the imaginative genre began at an early age thanks to some cool family friends while growing up in the Big Easy. "My brother went to college at Morehouse," he tells SPACE. "I was like 8, and he was 18. He’d always bring friends home, because New Orleans is a party city, so they'd come over and get drunk. But one of his friends gave me a book by Walter Mosley and one by Octavia Butler, and I got hooked into sci-fi and the future." "From 'Back to the Future' to 'Aliens,' the future was such an idea of what was going to be out there. Now we’re living it," reveals Mackie. "It’s very important to me as a human being to have that construct as a part of my career. The only thing more arrogant than wanting to be president is standing up and saying, 'Yeah, I can go to space.' That sounds crazy to me." "Exoplanet" was released by Audible on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: Audible) Leguizamo's New York City childhood was influenced by absorbing classic radio dramas of the past, which primed him for this special Audible project. “It was Anthony and Ariana being in it that really pumped me up, and of course Andy Weir," he recalls regarding his portrayal of Science Officer Logan Bowers. "Then when I got the theme, that it was something relevant today and makes you think about computers and technology taking over and making us obsolete. It just hit me in that right zeitgeist, at that right little point." "As a poor kid, there was no YouTube or cell phones, and we didn’t have computers," reminisces Leguizamo. "I used to go to the Broadcast Museum on 53rd Street and listen to old radio plays like The Shadow and these incredible detective radio plays. It's a different art form. With no visuals, your voice has to create the world. I thought that was an incredible challenge." DeBose portrays the Wild Blue Yonder's confident First Officer Becca Bang, who’s stranded in a temporal mystery that might engulf her at any moment. "I've yet to do anything like this, which is always exciting," she adds. "I was a little afraid of it, which told me I should do it. These gents are so talented. It's great company. It’s coming from brilliant minds who build worlds so impeccably. And it's about real stuff we’re dealing with today. I liked the idea that we could tell this story and make people listen and create a space for them to imagine themselves in it and see how they problem-solve to make the world a bit better." Recording your character's lines is far more difficult than just stepping up to the microphone to read a script, and our ace "Exoplanet" trio delivered in every session. "I just go in and throw myself at something," DeBose recalls. "I don’t really have a method. But I can tell you this: it is a full-body workout. I use everything at my disposal, whether it’s a chair or a pillow or running in place. I just do what the character does and end up sweating. And after three days, I have to go sit in silence. It's great. I love the idea of bringing back the radio play. The art of listening is such a thing. I don’t think people listen enough. Even for myself." "Exoplanet" revives the lost art of full-cast audio dramas for a new geneation (Image credit: Audible) Likewise, Leguizamo embraced his booth sessions with exuberance and authenticity. "You have to cancel the rest of your day, especially if you've got to talk, because your vocal chords are fried," he admits. "And if they're not fried you're not doing your job. You really have to do the physicality. If you run you have to run like a maniac and be out of breath. If I'm getting hit I start punching myself. Then there’s a sexiness to doing these things. Your voice has to have a little mystery, a little naughtiness. It’s an interesting intersection where you pull it back a little and invite the audience in.” For Mackie, who’s used to athleticism needed to play MCU superheroes like The Falcon and Captain America, recording dialogue offered a different type of opportunity. “I look for reasons not to talk to people, so I love doing these," he jokes. "Once I’m out of the studio, I’m not talking to anybody for two days. At a certain point for me, I find mentally I get tired of hearing myself talk. I just have to come home at cut off. I’ve said enough words for the next month.” "Exoplanet" is available now exclusively from Audible. One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone. A sci-fi thriller executive produced by Andy Weir (#1 bestselling author of Project Hail Mary, The Martian ), with an all-star cast led by Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose and John Leguizamo. Exoplanet is free for Audible members, but also available for purchase separately. View Deal
summary: Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo reveal why they joined Andy Weir's sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' (interview).

title: Football Daily: Squad number list sparks debate over missing football legends
content: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Forget about Michael Carrick. Don’t dwell on Women’s Bigger Cup. Fret not about Pierre Sage. No, the big football story of the day is Big Website’s Ultimate 1-50, a rundown of the male footballers best associated with each squad number. It’s lighthearted reading designed to entertain, maybe even inform, and perhaps spark a few memories and a touch of debate. Or, if you prefer, a rage-bait waste of time that shames the internet. Where the hell is Roy Keane! How dare you leave out Bobby Moore! And Pelé? A list without Pelé? I don’t want to live in a world where there are lists without Pelé. Such is the world these days, though surely a certain amount of respect is due to an exercise that shuns Lionel Messi and Zinedine Zidane but can welcome in Salvatore Sirigu and Mateusz Klich. And true, it might be a challenging read for those (and, let’s be clear, we’re absolutely definitely not referring to ourselves here, no sirree) old enough to have been brought up in an era of 1; 2, 5, 6, 3; 7, 4, 8, 11; 9 (big man), 10 (little man). The days of two substitutes who wore Nos 12 and 14. The days of a quarter of wine gums in your pocket and misty rain drifting across the floodlights and … oh my god Asamoah Gyan is wearing No 3 and playing up front. This is not a drill. Repeat this is not a drill. Burn it all down, the game’s gone. There is something about it all that does invoke strangely strong reactions, but every day is a school day. So, yes, there remains a hallowed aura around 1-11 but even some of the game’s greats – we’re looking at you Gerd Müller and Johan Cruyff – are best associated with numbers outside of the traditional undectet. And, as Jonathan Wilson brilliantly illustrates here, there’s a risk of being a bit Eurocentric when it comes to numbering – Argentina’s tactical evolution, for example, meant their traditional back four lines up 4, 2, 6, 3, with the No 5 in central midfield. Brazil too has No 5 as the defensive midfielder, with the standard back four as 4, 2, 3, 6. And don’t get us started on Hungary at Wembley in 1953 – Nandor Hidegkuti, you rascal! So do yourself a favour and dig into today’s offering. You might learn something. Or you might just get really, really cross about Curtis Jones. Either way, it’s win-win. Appreciate it’s all highly subjective but quite how you can give the all-time No 17 shirt to Kevin De Bruyne without so much as a mention of the legendary Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu is beyond me. What other player has gone from non-league to Premier League with the same club? OK, it’s a bit niche but a far more worthy winner in my completely unbiased (honest guv) opinion” – Kev Goddard. All this talk of 4-4 draws ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) is very intoxicating for Chesterfield fans of a certain vintage. First up, the 1992 draw at Anfield where we threw away a 4-1 lead after a Liverpool comeback inspired by Istvan Kozma (no, really). Dave Lancaster scored two that night and observed that he had thought beforehand there might be eight goals in it, but not that we’d score four of them. And then in 2004 at Saltergate against Grimsby, where we threw away a 3-2 lead to go 4-3 down, before equalising with a last-minute penalty thanks to David Reeves. The attendance that day was 4,444. Makes you think …” – David Ede. To stop managers continually going outside their technical areas, why not erect a ‘banners and poles’ surround, the sort of thing you see on pavements outside pubs and cafes? If the idea sounds a bit too simple, just mention the opportunity of more advertising space” – Peter Storch. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions.
summary: A new list ranking male footballers by their best-associated squad numbers has ignited online debate regarding the exclusion of players like Roy Keane and Pelé. The article highlights how numbering traditions vary globally, noting that Argentina and Brazil use different formations for their back four and midfield roles.
author: Guardian Sport

title: McTominay reveals heart shock treatment before Scotland World Cup opener
content:
Scott McTominay has disclosed that he was hospitalized for a cardiac procedure just two days before Scotland’s World Cup opener against Haiti. The midfielder stated he required a “shock on my heart” while in the United States as the team prepared for the match at Boston Stadium. Although his absence from training was initially attributed to a stomach complaint, it emerged in August that the Napoli player needed surgery to address an irregular heartbeat.

The actual operation was performed in September, resulting in McTominay missing Scotland’s first four Nations League matches. His recent revelation clarifies the timeline of his medical treatment, linking the initial hospitalization during the World Cup preparation period to the subsequent surgical intervention.
summary: Scott McTominay disclosed he underwent a heart shock procedure in a US hospital 48 hours before Scotland's World Cup match against Haiti. The Napoli midfielder had previously missed four Nations League matches due to surgery for an irregular heartbeat.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rio Ngumoha aims England start in Nations League as he declares Ballon d’Or goal
content:
Rio Ngumoha has said he is ready to make an impact for England, claiming he could become the best player in the world. The 18‑year‑old Liverpool winger, who narrowly missed selection for last summer’s World Cup squad, impressed during the pre‑tournament camp in Florida and has since forced his way into Thomas Tuchel’s plans after a strong start to the season.

With Bukayo Saka injured and several experienced players omitted from the Nations League squad, Ngumoha sees a chance to advance his case. He is described as dangerous on both flanks and could be selected for the upcoming match against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

Ngumoha also expressed a desire to test himself against Lamine Yamal when England face Spain in Madrid on Sunday, hoping to cement his place in the national team.
summary: Rio Ngumoha aims England start in Nations League as he declares Ballon d’Or goal.

title: Australian apprentice jockey Izzy Neale dies after fall at regional track
content: Twenty-two-year-old suffered severe injuries at race on Sunday ‘Words are not enough,’ says trainer Richard Freedman Apprentice jockey Izzy Neale has died following a fall at a regional racecourse. Neale suffered severe injuries when her mount Marnoo fell entering the home straight in the Warren Shire Cotton Cup in NSW.
summary: Twenty-two-year-old apprentice jockey Izzy Neale died after suffering severe injuries when her horse Marnoo fell entering the home straight in the Warren Shire Cotton Cup in NSW. Trainer Richard Freedman stated that words are not enough to describe the loss of the dearly loved rider.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Will Joseph poised to audition for leading role against Japan in Feyi-Waboso’s absence
content:
England are preparing to invite Gloucester winger Will Joseph to audition for a prominent position against Japan on Saturday, following the injury to star wing Manny Feyi-Waboso. The 24-year-old, who served as a travelling reserve for last weekend’s match against Australia, appears set for a Test recall four years after receiving his debut from current head coach Eddie Jones.

The selection move is part of a broader back-line reshuffle necessitated by several injuries, which have forced Steve Borthwick to reconsider the team composition that performed well against the Wallabies. Joseph has been in outstanding club form, and his brother Jonathan was a regular in England’s midfield for years. Additionally, Kevin Sinfield has stated that collaboration with clubs will be key to addressing these squad challenges.
summary: Will Joseph poised to audition for leading role against Japan in Feyi-Waboso’s absence.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Vikings acquire Kirk Cousins from Raiders for 2027 third-round pick
content:
The Minnesota Vikings have acquired veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders, according to reports from ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. In exchange for Cousins, the Vikings sent a third-round pick in the 2027 draft to Las Vegas. This move marks Cousins’ return to Minnesota after six seasons with the team.

Concurrently, the Raiders will hand their starting quarterback position to Fernando Mendoza, who is set to make his first NFL start. The trade occurred during the 2026 NFL trade deadline, reshaping the quarterback situations for both franchises.
summary: The Minnesota Vikings have acquired veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round pick in the 2027 draft. The Raiders are set to hand the starting job to Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick, who will make his first NFL start.
author: Guardian Sport

title: World Cup finalists England still feel short of best
content: England advanced to the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup final following an 86-18 victory over Australia. Despite the decisive win, try-scorer Rob Hawkins stated that the team has not yet reached its peak form.
summary: England are into the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup final after thrashing Australia 86-18 - but still have not hit peak form, according to try-scorer Rob Hawkins.

title: Credit Card Balances Rise $22B in Q3 as Democrats Push to Cap Rates
content: New data from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York indicates that Americans’ credit card balances rose by $22 billion, or 1.7 percent, in the third quarter compared to the second quarter. This increase in debt coincides with efforts by some Democratic lawmakers to cap interest rates.
